info.title: WrenDNS API
info.description: Read and control a WrenDNS resolver. JSON is camelCase; field names carry units (`totalMs`, `ttlSeconds`). Errors are RFC 9457 problem+json with a stable `code` and a `hint`. Time parameters take RFC 3339 or a relative offset (`-24h`). Collections page with `cursor`/`limit`. Analytics calls take `scope` (`cluster` or `node:local`; both mean this node until clustering is available).

get.description:
Part of the Pi-hole compatible API. The query string picks the call, as in Pi-hole v5, with
the token as `auth`: `summaryRaw` and `summary` (the 24 hour totals), `status`, `topItems`
(`topItems=N`: the top permitted and blocked names), `enable`, and `disable` or
`disable=<seconds>` (the same pause as `POST /api/v1/blocking/pause`; no number pauses for the
longest allowed, default 60 minutes). `versions` needs no token. Without a valid token a read
answers `[]` and a write 401; the API being off answers as any unknown page does. Prefer v6: v5 puts the
token in the address, which proxies and logs may keep.

200.description: Pi-hole v5's answer for the call.

401.description: A write without a valid token.

get.description:
Part of the Pi-hole compatible API. With a live `X-FTL-SID` answers
`{"session": {"valid": true, "validity": 300}}` and renews it; 401 otherwise.

401.description: No valid session.

post.summary: Pi-hole v6: sign in (the token is the `password`).
post.description:
Part of the Pi-hole compatible API (off unless an admin turned it on). Takes
`{"password": "<token>"}` and answers `{"session": {"valid": true, "sid": ..., "csrf": ...,
"validity": 300}}`; send `sid` as `X-FTL-SID` afterwards. 401 for a wrong password, 429 after
repeated failures, the ordinary 404 when the API is off.

401.description: Wrong password.

404.description: The API is off.

delete.summary: Pi-hole v6: sign out.
delete.description: Part of the Pi-hole compatible API. Ends the session named by `X-FTL-SID`; 204.

get.summary: Pi-hole v6: whether blocking is on.
get.description:
Part of the Pi-hole compatible API (needs a v6 session). `{"blocking": "enabled" | "disabled" |
"unknown", "timer": <seconds left or null>}`: disabled while any node has blocking paused for
everyone (the same state as `GET /api/v1/blocking`).

401.description: No valid session.

post.summary: Pi-hole v6: turn blocking off for a while, or back on.
post.description:
Part of the Pi-hole compatible API (needs a v6 session). `{"blocking": false, "timer": 300}`
pauses blocking for everyone for the timer's seconds (rounded up to whole minutes; no timer
pauses for the longest allowed, default 60 minutes; a longer timer is cut to it), the same
pause as `POST /api/v1/blocking/pause`. `{"blocking": true}` ends every pause. Answers like
`GET /api/dns/blocking`. Audit-logged as `blocking.pause` / `blocking.resume` by
`token:pihole-api`.

400.description: No `blocking` boolean.

401.description: No valid session.

get.description:
Part of the Pi-hole compatible API (needs a v6 session). Our version as the `core`, `web`
and `ftl` local versions; the remote (latest) versions are empty, so no update is offered.

401.description: No valid session.

get.description:
Part of the Pi-hole compatible API (needs a v6 session). The last 24 hours: `queries` (total,
blocked, `percent_blocked`, cached, forwarded, `unique_domains`, types, status, replies),
`clients` (active, total) and `gravity.domains_being_blocked`, in Pi-hole's shape.

401.description: No valid session.

get.description:
Part of the Pi-hole compatible API (needs a v6 session). The busiest devices over the last 24
hours (`count`, default 10, at most 100): `{"clients": [{"ip", "name", "count"}],
"total_queries", "blocked_queries"}`; names and addresses follow the node's privacy level.

401.description: No valid session.

get.description:
Part of the Pi-hole compatible API (needs a v6 session). `blocked=true` ranks blocked names,
otherwise the permitted ones; `count` (default 10, at most 100). Over the last 24 hours:
`{"domains": [{"domain", "count"}], "total_queries", "blocked_queries"}`.

401.description: No valid session.

get.description:
Part of the Pi-hole compatible API (needs a v6 session). Each configured upstream as
`{"ip", "name", "port", "count", "statistics": {"response", "variance"}}` (`count` is the
requests sent since start; `response` the smoothed answer time in seconds), with
`forwarded_queries` and `total_queries`.

401.description: No valid session.

put.summary:
REQ: DNS-014, API-901 (T27.14h, ADR-1098 point 4) — `[access] allowed_networks`, the one list for
the whole cluster. Admins only; no agent token changes it.
put.description:
Who may use this resolver, and reach the web UI and the API. The list applies on every node within
seconds; a file that sets it wins. A list that leaves out the requester's own address is refused
(409 `would_disconnect_you`).

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

parameters.name: simulate
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — with `dryRun=true`: replay the query log over this window (`24h`,
`7d`; at most 7 days; `true` for `[simulate] default_window`) and report what the
change would have done to those queries (`simulation`). `auto`: only when
`[simulate] plans_by_default` is on.

parameters.name: simulateUntil
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — where the simulated window ends: RFC 3339 or relative (`-24h`).
Default now.

200.description: Applied (or, with dryRun, what would change; `warnings` names a public range).

403.description: Only an admin can change the allowed networks; agents are refused.

409.description: `set_by_file`, the list leaves out your own address (`would_disconnect_you`), or a cluster member's build does not know the allowed networks yet (`upgrade_required`).

422.description: A network is wrong.

delete.summary: Removes the allowed networks the API set (the files' list, or the defaults, apply again).
delete.description:
The list the configuration files give, or the built-in defaults (private ranges, CGNAT, link-local
and loopback), applies again on every node within seconds.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

parameters.name: simulate
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — with `dryRun=true`: replay the query log over this window (`24h`,
`7d`; at most 7 days; `true` for `[simulate] default_window`) and report what the
change would have done to those queries (`simulation`). `auto`: only when
`[simulate] plans_by_default` is on.

parameters.name: simulateUntil
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — where the simulated window ends: RFC 3339 or relative (`-24h`).
Default now.

403.description: Only an admin can change the allowed networks.

404.description: The API sets no allowed networks.

409.description: The list that would apply leaves out your own address (`would_disconnect_you`).

get.description:
The alerts firing at this moment and the last delivery to each destination (with its
error, if it failed). Rules are checked on the cluster's primary; on another node
`evaluating` is false. The destinations and rules themselves are configuration:
`GET /api/v1/config/entries?kind=alert_destination` and `kind=alert_rule`.

put.summary: Add or change an alert destination (OBS-010, T9.6).
put.description:
The body has the same fields as `[[alerts.destination]]` (the name comes from the path):
`{"type": "ntfy", "url": "https://ntfy.sh/my-topic"}`, or for email
`{"type": "email", "url": "smtp://smtp.gmail.com:587", "from": "me@gmail.com", "to":
["me@gmail.com"], "username": "me@gmail.com", "password_file": "/run/secrets/smtp"}`, or for
Pushover `{"type": "pushover", "token_ref": "pushover-app", "user_key_ref": "pushover-user"}`
(the `url` defaults to Pushover's own; optional `device`, `sound`, `priority_firing`
(default 0), `priority_resolved` (default -1)).
Secrets stay in files on the node (`token_file`, `password_file`, `user_key_file`) or in its
encrypted store (`token_ref`, `password_ref`, `user_key_ref` name a stored secret: 422 `secret_missing` when none has that
name): only the path or the name is sent, and a password in `url` reads `<redacted>` wherever
the destination is shown (API-014; send it back as it is to keep it, as long as the URL's host
is unchanged). Setting a file or a reference is an admin's (OPS-014).
A destination the config files define is overridden until this one is deleted; a credential
the files set for it stays as they set it: left out of the body, it is kept, and a body that
sets, replaces or removes it is refused (409 `set_by_file`).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

parameters.name: simulate
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — with `dryRun=true`: replay the query log over this window (`24h`,
`7d`; at most 7 days; `true` for `[simulate] default_window`) and report what the
change would have done to those queries (`simulation`). `auto`: only when
`[simulate] plans_by_default` is on.

parameters.name: simulateUntil
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — where the simulated window ends: RFC 3339 or relative (`-24h`).
Default now.

200.description: Applied (or, with dryRun, what would change).

409.description: `set_by_file`: the config files set this destination's credential, and they win.

412.description: The configuration changed since the If-Match version: re-read it and retry.

422.description: A field is wrong, a reference names no stored secret (`secret_missing`), or the configuration wouldn't be valid: problem+json says which.

delete.summary: Remove an alert destination (OBS-010, T9.6).
delete.description:
Rules that still send to it make the configuration invalid (422 says which). A destination
the config files define, with a credential they set, can't be hidden (409 `set_by_file`).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

parameters.name: simulate
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — with `dryRun=true`: replay the query log over this window (`24h`,
`7d`; at most 7 days; `true` for `[simulate] default_window`) and report what the
change would have done to those queries (`simulation`). `auto`: only when
`[simulate] plans_by_default` is on.

parameters.name: simulateUntil
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — where the simulated window ends: RFC 3339 or relative (`-24h`).
Default now.

404.description: No entry by that name.

409.description: `set_by_file`: the config files define it with a credential.

422.description: A rule still uses it.

post.summary: Send a test alert to one destination (OBS-010, T9.6).
post.description:
Sends a message marked as a test, from this node, and answers with what happened: `ok`, or
the destination's error (a wrong password, an unreachable server). Nothing is stored, but
the test is audited. Needs the operator role.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The destination.

404.description: No destination by that name.

put.summary: Add or change an alert rule (OBS-010, T9.6).
put.description:
The body has the same fields as `[[alerts.rule]]` (the name comes from the path):
`{"when": "upstream_down", "for_secs": 60, "to": ["phone"]}`. `when` is one of
`upstream_down`, `node_down`, `list_failing`, `anomaly`, `servfail_rate`,
`update_available`, `sync_lag`, `primary_unreachable`, `new_device`, `disk_full`, `plan_pending`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

parameters.name: simulate
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — with `dryRun=true`: replay the query log over this window (`24h`,
`7d`; at most 7 days; `true` for `[simulate] default_window`) and report what the
change would have done to those queries (`simulation`). `auto`: only when
`[simulate] plans_by_default` is on.

parameters.name: simulateUntil
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — where the simulated window ends: RFC 3339 or relative (`-24h`).
Default now.

412.description: The configuration changed since the If-Match version: re-read it and retry.

422.description: A field is wrong, or the configuration wouldn't be valid: problem+json says which.

delete.description:
An alert the rule has firing stops being tracked (no "Resolved" message is sent). A rule
the config files define is hidden until this override is deleted in turn.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name.

parameters.name: dryRun

parameters.name: simulate

`7d`; at most 7 days; `true` for `[simulate] default_window`) and report what the
change would have done to those queries (`simulation`). `auto`: only when

get.summary: Device anomalies: rate spikes, heavy volume to one domain, drift, beaconing (OBS-013).
get.description:
Each finding compares a device with its own learned baseline (after a learning period,
7 days by default) and carries the evidence: observed value, usual value ± spread, the
threshold, and the window. Findings are alert-only; WrenDNS never blocks on them.
Newest first. In a cluster every node's findings are included (each node learns from the
queries it answers), with `nodes` saying which found each. Each has a stable `id` for
acknowledging it (OBS-014); `acknowledged` says who did and when, and `acknowledged=false`
returns only the ones nobody has. A finding an anomaly mute matched (OBS-038) is left out
unless `muted=true`; it then carries `mutedBy`, the mute's name.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only findings whose window started after this (RFC 3339 or relative, default `-7d`).

parameters.name: acknowledged
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-014 — `false`: only findings nobody acknowledged; `true`: only acknowledged
ones. Default: both.

parameters.name: muted
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-038 — `true`: muted findings are listed too, each with `mutedBy`. Default:
they are left out, as they are from the badge and the alerts.

400.description: Invalid request: problem+json says which parameter and how to fix it.

post.description:
Marks findings as seen, by their `id` from `GET /analytics/anomalies`: the sidebar badge and
`acknowledged=false` stop counting them, and each shows who acknowledged it and when. In a
cluster the primary records it (any node forwards) and every node shows it within seconds,
including nodes that were down, when they reconnect. Acknowledging changes no configuration,
so it works in a GitOps-managed cluster too. Findings keep being reported as before.
Needs the operator role (agents: the `ops:anomalies` scope); audit-logged as `anomaly.ack`.

400.description: No IDs, too many, a malformed one, or a long note.

503.description: A replica that can't reach the primary.

post.summary: Take back acknowledgements of device anomalies.
post.description:
The findings count in the badge again. Same rules as acknowledging; audit-logged as
`anomaly.unack`.

200.description: How many acknowledgements were taken back.

400.description: No IDs, too many, or a malformed one.

503.description: A replica that can't reach the primary.

get.summary: Domains devices contacted for the first time (OBS-009).
get.description:
Each device's first-seen registrable domains (after its first day, so the initial learning
doesn't flood the feed), with a score for how machine-generated the name looks (DGA
likelihood, 0 to 1). Newest first. A device that contacts several high-scoring new domains
in an hour also shows up in `/analytics/anomalies` as `dga`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only domains first seen after this (RFC 3339 or relative, default `-24h`).

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: Only this device (its address).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many (default 200, at most 2000).

400.description: Invalid request: problem+json says which parameter and how to fix it.

get.description:
Blocked names that look like they shouldn't be, best first (at most `limit`, default 50):
`allowedAfterBlock` counts devices that got the name answered normally within 10 minutes of
a block (someone paused blocking or allowed it: the strongest sign), `retryBursts` the times
a device asked for it 10 or more times within a minute while blocked (apps that break retry;
ad libraries do too, so weigh it lower). With the lists that blocked it. Since start; every
node's, merged by name. Names follow the query-log privacy level.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many (1–500, default 50).

get.summary: What the shadow lists would have blocked.
get.description:
A list with `mode = "shadow"` is compiled and checked but never blocks. For each query
answered normally, the telemetry thread checks it against the device's group's shadow lists
too; this is what they would have blocked since start: queries, devices, the names most
often, the last one. Every list in shadow mode is listed (with zero until it would block
something). Use it to judge a new list before turning it on. In a cluster, every node's
counts add up. Names follow the query-log privacy level.

200.description: One entry per list in shadow mode.

get.summary: Upstream answer quality and second opinions.
get.description:
Per node, per upstream since start: the DNSSEC verdicts on its answers (when validating),
the Extended DNS Error codes it returned (EDE 15 Blocked, 16 Censored, 17 Filtered mean the
upstream filters), and, when `[upstream_check] sample_every` is set, how sampled answers
compared with a second upstream's: `same`, `differentAddresses` (CDNs and geo-DNS answer per
resolver, usually harmless), `differentRcode`, `filtered` (one side had addresses, the other
none or only 0.0.0.0/loopback), or `unanswered`. `recent` lists the latest disagreements with
both answers. Names follow the query-log privacy level.

get.summary: Analytics over the query log in one query (`vqlog`, AGT-012).
get.description:
A small pipe language: `from -24h | where status = blocked and group = kids | top 10 name`,
`from -7d | where client = 192.168.1.20 | bucket 1h | stats count, p95(latency)`,
`where name under roku.com | by client | stats count, distinct(name)`. Stages: `from TIME
[to TIME]`, `where FIELD OP VALUE [and …]` (fields name, client, group, status, qtype,
rcode, upstream, proto, latency, `upstream_latency`; ops =, !=, in (…), not in (…), and for
names ~ glob, has, under; for latencies >, >=, <, <= in ms), `bucket 5m|1h|1d`, `by KEY,
…` (name, domain, client, group, status, qtype, rcode, upstream, proto), `stats count,
distinct(KEY), avg|min|max|p50|p90|p95|p99(latency|upstream_latency|answers|bytes)`, `top N
KEY`, `sort COLUMN [asc|desc]`, `limit N` (≤ 200). The answer is a table, the query as
understood, and its cost; `dryRun=true` only estimates. Never SQL; read-only. A query that
would read more than 100 million logged queries is refused with a 400 (narrow the time or
filter).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The query, for example `from -24h | where status = blocked | top 10 name`.
parameters.example: from -24h | where status = blocked | top 10 name

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Only parse and estimate the cost; don't scan.

400.description: Invalid request: problem+json says what's wrong in the query and how to fix it.

503.description: The query log is off.

get.description:
What was done to each node, or what it did to itself, newest first: configuration
versions applied (`seq`, `source`: `ui`, `api`, `agent`, `gitops`, `file`, or `cluster` on
a replica; `actor` when known), new builds, restarts, list refreshes that changed the rules,
rollout stages, maintenance, blocking paused or resumed, cache flushes, upstream circuit
breakers (at most one line per upstream per 5 minutes), and operators' and agents' notes.
Each node keeps its own (20,000 lines, 90 days); in a cluster every node is asked and each
marker carries its `node` (one change applied on four nodes is four markers with the same
`seq`). With `truncated`, ask again with `before = nextBefore` for older ones. Use it to
answer "what changed around then?". Example: `GET /api/v1/annotations?from=-6h&kinds=config.applied,note`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start (RFC 3339 or relative such as `-24h`; default 24 hours ago).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End (default now).

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.description: Kinds to keep, comma-separated (default all), e.g. `config.applied,note`.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: `cluster` (default, every node), `site:<name>`, `node:<name or ID>`, or `node:local`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many, newest first (1–2000, default 500).

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only markers before this time (RFC 3339): pass `nextBefore` from the previous page.

400.description: Invalid request: problem+json says which parameter and how to fix it.

post.summary: Leave a note on the time charts.
post.description:
Marks a moment on every time chart of every node with a short text, for what the network
itself can't see: "moved the access point", "ISP outage", "migrated the NAS". `time`
defaults to now and may be up to 7 days back. The receiving node keeps it (the federated
read shows it everywhere); it's not configuration, so it's allowed in a GitOps-managed
cluster. Notes can't be changed or deleted: add a correcting note. Needs the operator role
(agents: the `ops:annotate` scope); audit-logged as `annotation.note`.

403.description: Needs the operator role (agents: ops:annotate).

422.description: `annotation_text`: empty, over 200 characters, or several lines; `annotation_time`: ahead of now, or more than 7 days back.

put.summary: Mute kinds of device anomaly for some devices or groups (OBS-038).
put.description:
The body has the same fields as `[[anomaly_mute]]` (the name comes from the path):
`devices` (device names, IPs or CIDRs) and/or `groups`, `kinds` (`rate_spike`,
`domain_volume`, `drift`, `beacon`, `nxdomain_storm`, `dga`, `chatty_loop`), and optionally
`expires` (RFC 3339) and `note`, e.g. `{"devices": ["lg-tv-living"], "kinds":
["nxdomain_storm"], "expires": "2026-12-31T00:00:00Z", "note": "hourly PTR sweep"}`. A finding
a mute matches when it is created is still recorded and listed (`GET
/analytics/anomalies?muted=true`, with `mutedBy`), but isn't counted in
`wrendns_anomalies_total`, the badge, the `anomaly` alert rule, or the health level
(`wrendns_anomalies_muted_total` counts it). The same kind still counts for every other
device. The mute is shared: it applies on every node. There is no mute for everyone: name at
least one device or group.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

parameters.name: simulate
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — with `dryRun=true`: replay the query log over this window (`24h`,
`7d`; at most 7 days; `true` for `[simulate] default_window`) and report what the
change would have done to those queries (`simulation`). `auto`: only when
`[simulate] plans_by_default` is on.

parameters.name: simulateUntil
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — where the simulated window ends: RFC 3339 or relative (`-24h`).
Default now.

200.description: Applied (or, with dryRun, what would change).

412.description: The configuration changed since the If-Match version: re-read it and retry.

422.description: A field is wrong (no device or group, an unknown kind, a name that matches nothing, a MAC address), or the configuration wouldn't be valid.

delete.summary: Remove an anomaly mute (OBS-038).
delete.description: Findings created from now on count again; ones recorded while the mute held stay muted.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

parameters.name: simulate
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — with `dryRun=true`: replay the query log over this window (`24h`,

parameters.name: simulateUntil

put.description:
REQ: OBS-013 (T27.5, ADR-1007). Admin only for the telemetry sections; operators for the rest. Agents never.
The configuration files win field by field (`set_by_file`), and a field left out takes its default.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

parameters.name: simulate
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — with `dryRun=true`: replay the query log over this window (`24h`,
`7d`; at most 7 days; `true` for `[simulate] default_window`) and report what the
change would have done to those queries (`simulation`). `auto`: only when
`[simulate] plans_by_default` is on.

parameters.name: simulateUntil
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — where the simulated window ends: RFC 3339 or relative (`-24h`).
Default now.

200.description: Applied (or, with dryRun, what would change).

403.description: Not allowed for this role, or an agent.

409.description: `set_by_file`: a field the configuration files set.

422.description: A field is unknown or out of range.

delete.summary: Go back to the configuration file's `[telemetry.anomaly]` settings (ADR-1007).
delete.description: Removes what the API stored, so the file's settings apply again on every node (ADR-1007).

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

parameters.name: simulate
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — with `dryRun=true`: replay the query log over this window (`24h`,
`7d`; at most 7 days; `true` for `[simulate] default_window`) and report what the
change would have done to those queries (`simulation`). `auto`: only when
`[simulate] plans_by_default` is on.

parameters.name: simulateUntil
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — where the simulated window ends: RFC 3339 or relative (`-24h`).
Default now.

403.description: Not allowed for this role, or an agent.

404.description: Nothing was changed through the API: the file's settings are in effect already.

get.description:
Every change to users, passwords, two-factor sign-in, and API tokens, sign-ins and
lockouts, and configuration reloads, newest first, with who (attributed to the token and
its owner for API tokens), from where, why (`X-Wrendns-Reason`), and what changed. Append-only and
hash-chained; check it with GET /audit/verify.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Entries per page (1–500, default 100).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: From a previous page's `nextCursor`.

parameters.name: action

get.description:
Recomputes every entry's hash and link. `ok: false` with `firstBadSeq` means the log was
edited at or before that entry outside WrenDNS. Compare `headHash` with a value you
saved earlier to detect removed entries at the end.

post.description:
REQ: OBS-035 (T14.13) — exchanges a display link's code for a display session (a cookie),
from an address the display allows. The session reads only what the wall shows (the
statistics, the flow, the service level, the heatmaps, the change markers, the live tail),
lasts until the display is revoked or expires (no idle limit), and is checked against the
display's networks on every request. Failed codes count toward the address's sign-in
lockout. Audited as `display.open`.

401.description: The code isn't valid (revoked, expired, or mistyped).

403.description: Not from this address: the display is limited to some networks.

429.description: Too many failed attempts from this address.

post.description:
Username and password, plus `totp` (or `recoveryCode`) when two-factor sign-in is on:
without it the answer is 401 `totp_required`. Sets an `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict` session
cookie and returns the CSRF token to send as `X-CSRF-Token` on changes. Repeated failures
lock the username and the address out for a while (429). At most four password checks run
at once; beyond that the answer is 503 with Retry-After, which isn't a failed sign-in.

401.description: Not signed in, or the credentials are wrong.

429.description: Too many requests: wait for Retry-After seconds.

503.description: Busy checking other sign-ins: retry after Retry-After seconds (not counted as a failure).

post.description: Ends this session and clears the cookie. With a token or Basic, does nothing but succeed.

200.description: Signed out of an OIDC session: send the browser to `logoutUrl` to sign out at the provider too.

get.description:
The signed-in user: role (capped by a token's scope), two-factor state, unused recovery
codes, and how this request authenticated.

The provider returns here with `code` and `state`. Validates both, exchanges the code,
verifies the ID token, maps groups to a role (creating the user on first sign-in), sets
the session cookie, and redirects to the UI. Failures redirect to `/#/?loginError=...`.
Register `<public_url>/api/v1/auth/oidc/{id}/callback` with the provider.

parameters.description: Provider ID

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The authorization code from the provider.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The value WrenDNS sent at the start, checked against the sign-in cookie.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Set instead of `code` when the user cancelled or the provider refused.

parameters.name: error_description
parameters.description: The provider's explanation of `error`.

Redirects the browser to the provider (Authorization Code + PKCE). The provider sends it
back to `/api/v1/auth/oidc/{id}/callback`, which signs in and returns to `returnTo`.
Browsers only: link a "Sign in with ..." button here.

(`wrendns auth setup-token` prints it; the log names the file, not the token). Signs the

Confirms a current code from the app enrolled with POST /auth/totp/setup, turns
enforcement on, and returns ten single-use recovery codes (shown only now). Needs a signed-in session: API tokens and Basic credentials get 403.

get.summary: Download a backup of this node.
get.description:
One `.ttbk` file (ADR-063) with the configuration files, users and API tokens, devices and
names made through the API, the audit log, statistics history, and anomaly baselines.
Sign-in sessions, lists, and the cluster identity aren't included, and neither is the
query log (use `POST /api/v1/backup` with `includeQlog`, or `wrendns backup create
--include-qlog`, for that). **The stored secrets are left out** (they are encrypted with this
node's key, which no backup holds): `X-Wrendns-Backup-Secrets: omitted; count=N` says how
many. `POST /api/v1/backup` with a passphrase carries them. Restore it with
`wrendns backup restore FILE` on the new machine.

The file holds password hashes: keep it private. Admin only; audited as `backup.create`.

200.description: The backup, as an attachment named `wrendns-<node>-<time>.ttbk`.

X-Wrendns-Backup-Secrets.description: `omitted; count=N`: how many stored secrets were left out.

503.description: Backups aren't available on this node.

post.summary: Make a backup, optionally with the stored secrets.
post.description:
Like `GET /api/v1/backup` (one `.ttbk`; ADR-063), and with a body it can carry more:
- `includeQlog`: the query log too;
- `passphrase` (at least 12 characters): the node's stored secrets, encrypted under a key made
  from it (Argon2id m = 19 MiB, t = 2, p = 1; ChaCha20-Poly1305), as `data/secrets.enc`.
  The archive is then format 2, which builds before this one refuse. Restore needs the
  passphrase (`wrendns backup restore --secrets-passphrase-file`) or `--skip-secrets`.

`X-Wrendns-Backup-Secrets` says `included; count=N` or `omitted; count=N` (how many were left
out), and `X-Wrendns-Backup-Warnings` lists what to know (credentials held inline in the
configuration are copied as they are).

Admin only, never an agent token (403 `agent_not_allowed`), only over HTTPS or from the node
itself (403 `insecure_transport`). With a passphrase it needs an interactive session signed in
within the last 10 minutes: tokens and Basic sign-in get 403 `reauth_required`, with a hint to
run `wrendns backup create` on the node. One key derivation runs at a time: a second request
gets 429. On a cluster replica a passphrase is refused (409): make it on the primary, which
holds the same secrets and raises the alert. Audited as `backup.create` (`secretsIncluded`, `count`; never the passphrase), and
a backup with secrets raises the alert event `secrets_exported`. It takes no
`Idempotency-Key`: it changes no state.

200.description: The backup, as an attachment named `wrendns-<node>-<time>.ttbk`.

X-Wrendns-Backup-Warnings.description: Present when there is something to know; items separated by ` | `.

400.description: The body isn't valid, or the passphrase is under 12 characters, or the query log is too big for the API.

403.description: Not an admin, an agent token (`agent_not_allowed`), plain HTTP from another host (`insecure_transport`), or a passphrase without a recent sign-in (`reauth_required`).

409.description: A backup with a passphrase on a cluster replica: make it on the primary.

429.description: Another backup with a passphrase is deriving its key: wait for Retry-After seconds.

503.description: Backups aren't available on this node, or its secrets key can't be read (`secrets_locked`).

Needs the operator role (agents: the `ops:pause` scope); audit-logged as `blocking.pause`.

get.summary: The cache's top entries and makeup, per node.
get.description:
For each node: what its cache holds by kind (answers, NXDOMAIN, no data, SERVFAIL, stale,
DNSSEC-validated), and its `limit` entries with the most hits, the largest, or the fresh
ones closest to expiring. Each node walks its cache once for this (a few milliseconds per
100,000 entries, off the query path); looking doesn't count as a hit. A node that couldn't
be asked is listed with the error.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `hits` (default), `bytes`, or `expiring` (fresh answers closest to expiring).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Entries per node, 1 to 200 (default 25).

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: One node only (its site, pod, or ID); absent: every node.

post.summary: Flush the cache: one name, a subtree, one type, one kind, or everything; or the recursor's memory.
post.description:
With `name`, removes that name's cached answers (with `subtree`, every name under it too);
without, empties the cache. `type` (`A`, `AAAA`, `HTTPS`, `TYPE65`) keeps every other type,
for the name given or for every name. `kind` is `negative` (NXDOMAIN and no-data answers
only) or `bogus` (failed lookups: SERVFAIL, which is how a DNSSEC validation failure is
answered). `recursor` (`cuts`, `rtts` or `all`) instead empties what the built-in recursive
resolver remembers between queries: zone cuts and server addresses (the next lookup starts
from the root again) and each server's round-trip time; it can't be combined with the
others. By default every node in the cluster flushes; `node` limits it to one. The next
query for a flushed name is asked of the upstreams again. This doesn't clear devices' own
caches, blocked answers are never cached (unblocking needs no flush), and to change what a
name resolves to, use local names instead. Needs the operator role (or the `ops:cache`
agent scope); audit-logged as `cache.flush`.

set DO or CD), with the node that holds it, its response code, answer count, whether it was
DNSSEC-validated, how long it stays fresh (negative: how long it has been stale), its age,
size, and hits. Looking doesn't count as a hit or change anything. Blocked answers are never
cached, so they don't appear.

parameters.description: The name to look up, e.g. `www.example.com`.

For each node (this one first): entries, memory, hits, misses, the hit rate, stale answers
served, prefetches, evictions, and answers that couldn't be cached. Each node has its own
cache, so a cluster shows one row per node.

Every category the catalog offers, grouped as the picker shows them, with its description,
tiers, entry counts and weight; every source with its maintainer, licence (an SPDX
identifier and a link), format, size and cadence, and what this node has done with it
(downloaded or not, how big, any error); the presets (`basic`); the categories not offered
and why; what each group selects now and what all of them cost together (distinct sources
counted once), against the node's memory limit and `[filter] entry_budget`. In a cluster the
numbers are the primary's, which downloads and compiles. Needs `config:read` for an agent.

The body has the same fields as `PUT /api/v1/lists/{name}` (`name` optional): a `url` is

as they are, then parsed as the compiler would. Answers with the rules found, the lines it
couldn't use, and the time. Nothing is saved or compiled; the check is audited. `path`
lists are checked when saved. Needs the operator role (agents: `config:write:lists`).

post.description:
It needs an admin (agents never). A stored credential is sent only to the address and TLS settings
it was saved with: with another address the check runs without it (`credentialSent: false`), so a
stored key never goes to a new address (API-016, T23.8, ADR-922).

the form (API-016, T23.8, ADR-120).

builds it and asks it for the root's NS records, as health checks do, and answers with what
happened: `ok` with the rcode, records, and time, or the error (a bad URL, a TLS name that
doesn't match, a timeout). Nothing is saved; the check is audited. Needs the operator role
(agents: `config:write:upstreams`).

Per device, its queries on each node over the window and the share on its most-used one
(`mostly pi`, `both`). A device that has only used one server may still have a second one
configured: most systems use their first server until it stops answering. Run a drill to
find out. No finding, no alert, no health reason. Federated over every node's seen table.

parameters.description: `1d` to `7d` (default `7d`).

One row per device seen in the last day (every node's, in a cluster: the most confident
guess per device): the product (`Roku player`), its class (`streaming`), how sure
(`likely` from a score of 0.6, `possibly` from 0.35, else `unknown` with the MAC vendor
alone), the vendor, and `suggestedGroup` when a group's `device_classes` asks for it. A
device's `[[client]] kind` wins (`source: override`). Guessed from the MAC vendor, the names
the device announces, and the domains it talks to; it never changes how a query is
answered. Empty at query-log privacy level 1 and above, or with `[identify] enabled = false`.

get.summary: What one device looks like, and why (OBS-025).
get.description:
`id` is the device's address, or a named device's name (its first address). The answer
carries the evidence: the signature's domains the device talked to and their weights, the
MAC prefix and vendor, the announced name that matched, every name and domain seen, and a
runner-up within 0.1 ("could also be …"). `available: false` with `reason`: `disabled`,
`privacy_level`, or `not_seen` (no queries from it in the last day).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: An address, or a named device's name.

404.description: No named device by that name, and not an address.

get.description:
`id` is a configured device's name, an address, or a Kubernetes workload
(`namespace/kind/name`). The answer names the group the device lands in and the key that
matched (the precedence is client ID, MAC, workload, address, network, router name, default),
then lists what applies as `sections`: the block response, the group's lists and blocked
services, safe search, rewrites, schedules with whether each is in effect now, the quick and
group rules with their expiry, and the upstream group. It is resolved with the same
identification a query and `GET /explain` use, so the two agree. In a cluster a replica asks
the primary. Needs `config:read` for an agent.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A device's name, an address, or a workload.

404.description: Neither a configured device, an address, nor a known workload.

get.summary: How a device's queries are spaced (OBS-031).
get.description:
For each registrable domain the anomaly engine tracks for the device (up to 16 per node),
the gaps between its queries as counts in 24 log-spaced bins (`binsS`: under 1 s, then
1–1.5 s, 1.5–2.2 s, … up to 7,290 s and longer): `hour` (this hour) and `recent` (each hour's
close halves it and adds that hour). `dominantBin` and `dominantSharePct` say how regular it
is (a time-sync loop every 2.5 s puts nearly everything in bin 3, 2.2–3.3 s), `period` says it
in words, `knownPeriodic` that it was periodic while the device was learning (usual), and
`regularHours` how long the beacon detector has found it regular (4 reports a new beacon).
Every node's, summed by domain. `id` is an address, or a named device's name. Needs the
anomaly engine (`available: false`, `reason: disabled` without it), which runs only at
query-log privacy level 0. `bins=false` leaves the bins out. Example:
`GET /api/v1/clients/10.20.2.14/rhythm`.

parameters.description: An address, or a named device's name.

parameters.name: bins
parameters.description: `false`: the dominant period and share per domain without the bins (default true).

422.description: `privacy_level`: the query log's privacy level hides devices and names.

One device over a window (default the last 24 hours, at most 7 days) as swimlanes: a lane per
registrable domain (the top `lanes` by queries, the rest in `other`) with its queries, blocked
answers, and slow answers (over the latency objective's threshold) per bin (`bins`, whole
minutes; 288 by default, 5 minutes over a day); every query and the p99 answer time per bin
(the latency lane); `events`: domains first contacted, anomaly findings for the device, and
blocked bursts (10 or more blocked in a bin); and the change markers. From the query log, so
nothing older than it keeps (`coverageFrom`); every node's rows that reached this one. The
same request within 30 seconds is answered from memory. `truncated` says a read stopped
early. At privacy level 1 the lanes have no domain; from level 2 it's refused. Use it to
answer "when did this start, and what else did the device do?". Example:
`GET /api/v1/clients/10.20.2.14/timeline?from=-24h`.

that deviates from the others (`odd`: robust z ≥ 3 against the others' median and MAD with
three or more nodes, non-overlapping intervals with two) with the time it started
(`oddSince`), and `note`s a node that only looks worse because it has the same bad count on a

delete.summary: Remove a node from the cluster.
delete.description:
The primary drops the node from the member list (so it stops counting as a voter, and the
Cluster page and the `WrenDNSClusterPeerDown` alert stop listing it) and adds its ID to
the list of removed nodes that travels with every version: no node accepts a connection from
it again, even while its certificate is valid. The node's own data isn't touched. A node that
is up is removed only with `force=true`; the answer then says it was up. The primary can't
be removed, and neither can a node by site or pod name: use the ID the Cluster page shows.

If the node was eligible it holds a copy of the cluster key (`heldClusterKey`): removal
stops the cluster accepting its certificate, but if the node is lost or can't be trusted,
rotate the CA too (`wrendns cluster rotate-ca`). Removing a voter can leave fewer than three,
which turns automatic failover into manual (`automaticFailoverAfter`, and a note).

A replica sends the request to the primary. It changes no configuration, so a GitOps-managed
cluster takes it too. `?dryRun=true` runs every check and says what would happen. Admin
(agents: `cluster:admin`); audit-logged as `cluster.node.remove`.

get.summary: Whether Kubernetes workloads are on, and how the table is doing (FLT-017).
get.description:
`role`: `watching` (this node lists and watches pods and namespaces), `peer` (it takes the
watcher's table over the cluster channel), `fixture` (a test file), or `off`. With
`lastSyncSecondsAgo` (the API server last confirmed the table, or a peer last sent it), the
table's size, the namespaces watched, and the last error until the next success. The health
level turns `degraded` (`kubernetes_stale`) when a watcher's table is older than 15 minutes;
DNS answers regardless.

One row per workload (`namespace/kind/name`, from its pods' owners: a Deployment's replicas
are one device across rollouts), sorted by name: its group and where that came from (a pod
label, a namespace label, a `[[kubernetes.map]]` rule, or `default_group`), its pods and
their addresses, queries and blocked answers in the last 24 hours (summed over every node in
a cluster; `missingNodes` lists nodes whose counts are missing), and when it last asked.
Every node holds the watcher's table, so the list itself never depends on one node. Use the
name or `key` as `client` anywhere a device goes: the query log, the timeline, rhythm,
identity. `kubernetes_disabled` (409) when the feature is off. Example:
`GET /api/v1/kubernetes/workloads?namespace=media`.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.description: Only this namespace.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Only workloads in this group (`none` for those without one).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many (default and maximum 200).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: From the previous page's `nextCursor`.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: `cluster` (default) or `node:local`: whose counts.

200.description: The workloads, a page at a time.

400.description: A bad cursor or scope.

409.description: `kubernetes_disabled`: no node watches the Kubernetes API.

get.summary: Filter lists and their download state.
get.description:
Every configured list with its kind (block/allow), source, download state (`ok`, `failed`,
`pending`) and last error, size, and how many names it contributes to the active snapshot;
when it was last checked, last confirmed current, and last changed, and whether a refresh is
queued or downloading it now (`refreshing`). `hits` adds up every node's in a cluster. On a
cluster replica the download state is the primary's (it downloads and compiles the lists
every node serves). `missingNodes` names the nodes whose hits are left out and, when the
primary doesn't answer, the primary (the download state shown is then this node's own).

get.summary: How much each filter list adds.
get.description:
Every enabled list with its entries, the names no other list of its kind has (`unique`:
what turning it off would lose), its modifier rules and regexes (counted as unique: overlap
is by name), what it adds as a share of its entries, the lists that cover the rest, and the
groups that name it. Counted while the lists are compiled, once per compile; a list not
compiled yet shows zeros. Names a block list and an allow list both have don't count as
shared.

post.summary: Turn off the lists that add little.
post.description:
Recomputes the plan for `thresholdPercent` and turns the lists in it off (`enabled = false`;
each stays in the configuration with its source, so turning it on again is one edit). With
`names` (the ones the person previewed), each must still be in the plan or nothing changes
(409: preview again). Needs the operator role and a person: agent tokens are refused
(`agent_not_allowed`); they read the plan. Audit-logged as `lists.prune`.

400.description: A malformed body, a threshold outside 0 to 50, or too many names.

403.description: Needs the operator role; agent tokens are refused.

409.description: A named list isn't in the plan any more: preview again.

get.summary: Which lists a prune would turn off.
get.description:
The block lists in enforce mode that add at most `thresholdPercent` (default 1) of their own
entries, least-adding first, chosen so that turning all of them off together still loses at
most that share of each; `kept` says why every other enabled list stays (an allow list, a
shadow list, a group names it, it adds more). `losesAtMost` is an upper bound on the names
that would stop being blocked. Changes nothing; the apply is `POST /api/v1/lists/prune`, for
a person.

parameters.name: thresholdPercent
parameters.description: Turn off lists adding at most this share of their entries, 0 to 50 (default 1).

400.description: A threshold outside 0 to 50.

post.description:
Downloads every enabled filter list again now (or only the lists in `names`), without
waiting for their `refresh_secs` schedule, like Pi-hole's "Update Gravity" (`pihole -g`).
Answers 202 at once with what was queued; the downloads run in the background, and
`refreshing` in `GET /api/v1/lists` is true until each list's download ends
(`lastSuccessUnixSeconds` then moves on). Unchanged sources cost one conditional request
each, and the filter snapshot is recompiled only when something changed (it then serves
within seconds). A failed download keeps the last good copy. Disabled lists are left out
(`skipped`). In a cluster the primary downloads and compiles the lists every node serves:
a replica forwards the request (503 when it can't reach the primary; replicas keep serving
the last lists). `?dryRun=true` says what would be queued and queues nothing.
`Idempotency-Key` replays the first answer for 24 hours. It changes no configuration (a
GitOps-managed cluster takes it too). Needs the operator role (agents: the
`config:write:lists` scope and a reason); audit-logged as `lists.refresh`.

parameters.description: Check and report without changing anything.

requestBody.description: Optional: `{}` or no body refreshes every enabled list.

404.description: No list by one of those names (the hint lists them).

409.description: This node doesn't download lists (`lists_not_here`: role resolver), or an Idempotency-Key reused for another request.

503.description: A cluster replica that can't reach the primary (it downloads the lists).

The network as a graph: the gateway, networks and VLANs, devices (the 200 busiest; the rest
fold into `+N more` per network), one resolver per WrenDNS node with its answer kinds, and
the upstreams. Edges carry the rate over the last 60 seconds and the shares of slow, failing and
blocked answers. Every node and edge has a `health`: `green`, `yellow`, `red`, or `idle` (too
few answers to say). The map is built from a sample of the lookups, never from the query path;
`sampleRate` says how thin the sample is. No domain name appears anywhere. `partial` and
`missingNodes` say when a cluster node didn't answer (it is a red resolver).

per second each node samples, 10 to 2,000), `min_sample` (answers before a device or edge is

thresholds `warn_slow_pct`, `warn_error_pct`, `error_pct` and `warn_blocked_pct` (1 to 100;
`error_pct` at least `warn_error_pct`). It replaces the whole section until it's deleted
again, on every node of a cluster, and applies within a few seconds with no restart.

get.description:
This node's country database for the world view: `enabled`, `state` (`off`, `missing`,
`downloading`, `ready`, `failed`), the source's month, when it was built, its size, when the
next check is due and the last error's code. The database is never bundled and is downloaded
only after an admin turns `[map.geoip]` on; each node that serves the console keeps its own
copy. Change the settings with `PUT /map-settings/default` (admin), fetch now with `POST
/map/geoip/update`, remove it with `DELETE /map/geoip`.

delete.description:
Removes this node's copy (and its `.prev`). While `[map.geoip]` stays on nothing is fetched
again until an admin presses Update now or turns it off and on; the world view says
`geoip_missing`. Admin only (never an agent); audited as `map.geoip.delete`.

Starts a download on this node, in the background, even when the day's check is not due (it
also lifts a "Delete database"). The status shows `downloading`, then `ready` or `failed` with
the error's code; a failed fetch keeps the old database. Admin only (never an agent); audited
as `map.geoip.update`. 409 `conflict` when a fetch is running or the toggle is off.

busiest flows. Device names appear only at privacy levels 0 and 1 (at 2 and above devices are
hidden). The same data as the MCP tool `network_health`.

unfiltered: filter it on your side) and a `ping` event every 15 seconds. One ticker builds the
snapshot for every subscriber and stops when the last one leaves. At most 8 streams per node
(`429 map_streams_busy`) and at most 2 per user or token. When the map is turned off the stream sends a `map_disabled` event and ends. Close it when the page is hidden.

404.description: `map_disabled`.

429.description: `map_streams_busy`: 8 streams are open on this node.

Countries with the rate, count and slow share of the answers that point there, and a marker
for each upstream whose address has a country. `available: false` with a `reason` when
answers can't be placed: `geoip_off` or `geoip_missing` (the GeoIP database, `GET
/map/geoip`), `address_not_recorded` (the lookup's answer address isn't kept yet, ADR-970: the
upstream `markers` are then where the upstreams are, not where answers point) or `privacy`
(level 3 keeps nothing per event). `unlocated` counts the answers with no place: failed,
blocked and local ones, and prefixes with no country. Countries come from the database of the
node that answers.

The LANs and VLANs your routers report (`[[router]]`, UniFi: subnet, VLAN, DHCP pool,
domain), then any client group's `networks` that no router reported. Each with the group
that covers it and how many known devices are in it (the routers' DHCP clients, Home
Assistant's devices, and mDNS names), so you can see which networks are filling up. Read
where the routers are read: a replica asks the primary and adds the networks it is directly
on; with the primary away it answers from its own data and `missingNodes` names the primary.

get.description:
The cache, support and updates settings it runs with, the fields the files set, and whether a
restart is still pending for them. Its `node` is the name the `*-settings/{node}` routes take.

The cache, support and updates settings in effect there, the fields the files set, and whether a
restart is still pending for them. 404 when no node of the cluster has that ID.

parameters.description: The node ID.

get.summary: The drill running on a node.
get.description:
Its targets, reason, time left, and how many queries (from how many devices) it hasn't
answered so far. 404 when none runs.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: `local`, or a node's ID, site, or pod name.

404.description: No drill runs there (or no such node).

post.summary: Start a failover drill on a node.
post.description:
For `forSecs` (15 to 300, default 60) the node stops answering its `targets` (`"all"`,
`{"clients": [...]}` with addresses, device names, or Kubernetes workloads, or
`{"group": "iot"}`): UDP queries get no answer and stream connections are closed, the
nearest thing to a dead node, counted as status `drilled`. It's a maintenance window too
(not ready, alerts muted, out of elections; on the primary, `handover` hands the role over
first). The node's infrastructure, cluster nodes, loopback, and excluded devices are always
answered. Every node records who asks it during the drill; 60 seconds after the end the
drilled node merges them into a report (`GET /api/v1/drills/{id}`). Refused (409
`drill_refused`, the reason in the detail) when no other node is ready and answering, the
node is in maintenance, a drill ran in the cluster in the last 10 minutes, a rollout is
pinned or baking, or health is `severe`; 409 `drill_active` while one runs; 422
`drill_targets` for an unknown group, no device seen in the last hour, or a bad length or
reason. A restart cancels a drill. `?dryRun=true` returns the checks, the baseline, and the
devices without dropping anything. Not a configuration change: a GitOps-managed cluster
takes it too. Needs the operator role (agents: the `ops:drill` scope, which no token gets by
default); audit-logged as `drill.start`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: `local`, or a node's ID, site, or pod name.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Only check the preconditions and resolve the targets; nothing is dropped.

200.description: A dry run: the checks, the baseline, and the devices.

404.description: No such node (`node_unknown`).

409.description: A precondition refuses it (`drill_refused`), or one is running (`drill_active`).

422.description: Unusable targets, length, or reason (`drill_targets`).

503.description: The node isn't reachable over the cluster channel (`node_unreachable`).

delete.summary: End a node's drill early.
delete.description:
The node answers its targets again at once and leaves the maintenance window; the report
still runs 60 seconds later. 404 when no drill runs there. Needs the operator role (agents:
`ops:drill`); audit-logged as `drill.end`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: `local`, or a node's ID, site, or pod name.

200.description: The drill that ended (`until` is now).

404.description: No such node, or no drill running there.

503.description: The node isn't reachable over the cluster channel (`node_unreachable`).

post.description:
For `forSecs` (60 to 86,400; agents at most 7,200; default the node's
`[node] maintenance_default_secs`, 3,600) the node answers `/readyz` with 503 so load
balancers and Kubernetes stop sending it new queries, while every DNS listener keeps
answering whatever still arrives. Its alerts and health conditions are left out, and it
doesn't stand in elections, until the window ends (by itself, or with DELETE). The window
survives a restart. Starting again replaces the window. `id` is `local` (the node answering)
or a cluster node's ID, site, or pod name: the request goes to that node over the cluster
channel. On the primary under automatic failover, `handover` (default true) hands the primary
role to another eligible node first (configuration changes pause for about 30 s); otherwise
the primary keeps the role and the answer's `note` says to promote another node first. It
changes no configuration, so a GitOps-managed cluster takes it too. Needs the operator role
(agents: the `ops:maintenance` scope); audit-logged as `node.maintenance.start`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: `local`, or a node's ID, site, or pod name.

200.description: The node's window, and what happened to the primary role.

404.description: No such node (`node_unknown`).

422.description: No reason, or a window too short or too long (`maintenance_invalid`, `maintenance_too_long`; agents at most 2 h).

503.description: The node isn't reachable over the cluster channel (`node_unreachable`).

delete.summary: End maintenance on a node.
delete.description:
The node is ready again at once (if it's otherwise ready), and alerts and the health level
cover it again: conditions that hold count from now, so an alert with `for_secs` waits its
usual time. Nothing happens if it wasn't in maintenance. `id` as for starting. Needs the
operator role (agents: `ops:maintenance`); audit-logged as `node.maintenance.end`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: `local`, or a node's ID, site, or pod name.

200.description: The node, no longer in maintenance.

404.description: No such node (`node_unknown`).

503.description: The node isn't reachable over the cluster channel (`node_unreachable`).

get.summary: The OIDC sign-in providers in the configuration, with their status on this node.
get.description:
Each provider comes with its settings (the client secret as a name, never a value), where it
comes from (the files or the API), and whether this node serves its sign-in button: a node
without `[auth.oidc] public_url`, or one that can't read the provider's secret or reach its
issuer, shows it as inactive with the reason (API-016). Admins only.

403.description: Only an admin can read the sign-in providers.

put.summary: Add or change an OIDC sign-in provider.
put.description:
API-016 (T23.10, ADR-903 §6, ADR-967). The body has the fields of `[[auth.oidc.provider]]`
(the ID comes from the path): `issuer`, `client_id`, `name`, `scopes`, the claims and the role
rules. The client secret is a name, never a value: `client_secret_ref` names a stored secret
(422 `secret_missing` when none has that name); `client_secret` and `client_secret_file` are
set in the configuration file, not through the API. Admins only: an operator or an agent is

get.description:
Newest first. Filters combine with AND: name (substring by default; `match=exact|suffix|
glob|regex`), client, status, query type, response code, upstream, minimum latency, and
time range. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for older rows. Example:
`GET /api/v1/queries?name=doubleclick&status=blocked&from=-1h&limit=50`. To keep what a
filter does NOT match, add `nameNot`, `clientNot`, `statusNot`, `qtypeNot`, or `rcodeNot`
(`=true`): `?name=doubleclick&nameNot=true&from=-1h` is every query in the last hour whose
name does not contain `doubleclick`. A negated search reads every block the time range and
the other filters leave, so give a time range or another filter on a long log.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name to look for; see `match`.

parameters.name: match
parameters.description: How to match `name`. Default: `substring`.

parameters.name: nameNot
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-003 (ADR-171) — keep the rows whose name does NOT match `name` and `match`:
does not contain, is not, is not under, doesn't match the wildcard or the regex. Needs
`name`. Default: false.

parameters.name: client
parameters.description:
Client IP address, or several, comma-separated (REQ: OBS-003, ADR-1013): addresses,
`hostname:<label>` (the addresses a router gave that name now) and Kubernetes workloads
(`namespace/kind/name`). At most 100 entries and 256 addresses; `clientTruncated` says
when a cap cut the set.

parameters.name: clientNot
parameters.description: Keep the rows from every client except `client` (all of them, when several). Needs `client`. Default: false.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Statuses, comma-separated (`blocked,forwarded`).

parameters.name: statusNot
parameters.description:
Keep the rows whose status is none of `status` (`status=blocked&statusNot=true`: every
query that was not blocked). Needs `status`. Default: false.

parameters.name: qtype
parameters.description: Query types, comma-separated (`A,AAAA`).

parameters.name: qtypeNot
parameters.description: Keep the rows whose type is none of `qtype`. Needs `qtype`. Default: false.

parameters.name: rcode
parameters.description: Response codes, comma-separated (`NXDOMAIN,SERVFAIL`).

parameters.name: rcodeNot
parameters.description:
Keep the rows whose response code is none of `rcode` (queries that got no response code
are kept). Needs `rcode`. Default: false.

parameters.name: upstream
parameters.description:
Upstream ID (from `/upstreams`): the forwarded queries it answered. Coalesced queries
name the upstream that answered for all of them.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Only queries from devices in this group (a group name, ADR-050).

parameters.name: minLatencyMs
parameters.description: Only queries that took at least this long.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start: RFC 3339 or relative (`-1h`). Default: no limit.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End. Default: now.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page (1–1000, default 100).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Continue after a previous page (`nextCursor` from it).

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description:
`cluster` (default, every node), `site:<name>`, `node:<name or ID>`, or `node:local`
(this node). Federated reads list nodes that didn't answer in `missingNodes`.

parameters.description:

on `/metrics` or an exported trace). Replaces `from` and `to`.

get.description:

asked (cut down by QNAME minimization), the outcome (`referral`, `answer`, `nodata`,
`nxdomain`, `lame`, `timeout`, `error`, `case-mismatch`), the delegation a referral points to,
the transport and the time. A name whose zone cuts are cached starts below the root; flush the
resolver's cuts (`POST /api/v1/cache/flush` with `recursor`) to see the whole walk. The lookup
is real: answers are not stored in the answer cache, but the resolver's zone cuts and server
timings are updated. Example: `GET /api/v1/recursor/trace?name=www.example.com`.

router (`api_key_file`, `api_secret_file`, `password_file`, `tls_ca`): those are set in the
configuration file. Admins only: an operator or an agent is refused (403).
A router the config files define is read-only here (409 `set_by_file`).

get.summary: List the stored secrets (never a value).
get.description:
Every stored secret with its kind, stamp, who set it when, the credential fields that name it
(`usedBy`), and which nodes hold it and can read it; names a reference uses that aren't set
come with `set: false`. Also this node's secrets store (ready, locked and why, the key's
source and ID: never the key) and every credential field of this node's configuration with
its source: `inline` or `file` (the configuration files set it, and win: the UI shows it
read-only), or `stored`, and whether this node can read it. On a replica the list is the
primary's when it answers, otherwise this node's with `stale: true`. The answer's `ETag` is the
secrets head, for `If-Match` on a write. Operators and admins; agents with `config:read`
(MCP `secrets_status`).

put.summary: Set (or replace) a stored secret.
put.description:
Stores `value`, encrypted with the node's key, under `name` (lowercase letters, digits, `.`,
`_` and `-`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 63). Entries name it in their `*_ref`
fields (`api_key_ref = "unifi"`). The value is write-only: the answer, every read, the audit
entry (`secret.put`: name, kind, stamp, users) and the logs hold only metadata. In a cluster a
replica sends it to the primary (`secret.put` over the cluster channel); pins and staged
rollouts don't hold it back, and a configuration managed in Git doesn't refuse it (secrets
are state, never in Git). Refused on an emergency primary, a primary without its lease, or
with no primary reachable (409).

Admins only: agent tokens get 403 `agent_not_allowed`, whatever their scopes. Only over HTTPS
or from the node itself (403 `insecure_transport`; `[api] allow_secrets_over_http` lifts it).
`?dryRun=true` checks the name, kind and value and reports `wouldCreate`/`wouldReplace` and the
fields that would become configured, storing nothing. `Idempotency-Key` replays the first
answer for the same value (another value with the same key is 409); `If-Match` takes the
secrets head's `ETag` (412 when it moved).

Kind `pem` (PEM blocks, with their line breaks) is for WrenDNS's own listeners: admin only, once
every cluster member's build knows it (409 `upgrade_required`, naming the member), and its value
is never returned by any API, MCP, `ctl`, log, support package or backup. The names the
certificate issuer keeps (`acme.account`, `cert.<name>.key`, `cert.<name>.chain`,
`cert.cluster.key`, `cert.cluster.chain`) are refused with 409, whatever the kind.

409.description: No primary to take it, an emergency primary or one without its lease, a primary too old to store secrets (`upgrade_required`), the configuration files set that credential (`set_by_file`), or an Idempotency-Key reused with another value.

post.summary: What a candidate configuration would have done (OBS-024).
post.description:
The body's `config` is a shared configuration as JSON: the sections a cluster replicates,
as a Git commit's `wrendns/shared.toml` becomes (`wrendns config simulate` reads the TOML
and sends this). Node-local sections are ignored: this node's own apply. Each logged query
over `window` (default `[simulate] default_window`, at most 7 days; newest first, at most
`[simulate] max_rows` rows and `max_secs` seconds) is decided again under the configuration
in effect and under the candidate, and the differences are counted: newly blocked, newly
allowed, a changed route, a changed answer, by name, device, and group. In a cluster every
node replays its own log (and the logs shipped to it) and the counts are summed; nodes that
didn't answer are in `missingNodes`. Nothing changes and nothing is audited. Needs the
viewer role (agents: `config:read` and `querylog:read`).

get.description:
The query flow as a diagram's data: groups → decision (status) → upstream → response code.
Each link is a counter incremented for exactly that pair as queries were answered (no
proportional split): `group:<name> → status:<label>` for every answer, then
`status → upstream:<name> → rcode:<name>` for answers an upstream was asked for and
`status → rcode` for the rest; a status or upstream whose `count` exceeds what leaves it
has `deadEnd` answers (dropped queries get no response code). Every node's, summed, from the
time buckets (`source: buckets`; `partial` when some lacked the counts). With `client`, one
device's flow from the query log over at most the last 24 hours (`source: querylog`;
`truncated` when the read stopped early); refused at privacy level 2 and above. Example:
`GET /api/v1/stats/flow?from=-6h`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start (RFC 3339 or relative; default 1 hour ago, or 24 hours for a device).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End (default now).

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: One device (its address): its flow from the query log, over at most the last 24 hours.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: `cluster` (default), `site:<name>`, `node:<name or ID>`, or `node:local`.

400.description: Invalid request: problem+json says which parameter and how to fix it.

422.description: `privacy_level`: the privacy level hides devices.

503.description: A device's flow needs the query log, which is off.

get.description:
For the whole network (exact, from the time buckets: hour slots back 400 days, 15-minute or
minute slots back 7 days), or for one device (`kind=client`, `key` its address) or one name
(`kind=name`) by hour, from each hour's top list of the busiest 100: exact while the key
is in the list; `covered` is false for hours where it wasn't (its count is unknown, not
zero). `starts` and `values` are parallel arrays in UTC; lay them out by local time. Every
node's, summed. A name needs privacy level 0 (names are hashes above it), a device level 1 or
lower. Example: `GET /api/v1/stats/heatmap?from=-7d&grain=15m`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start (RFC 3339 or relative; default 7 days ago).

parameters.name: to

`hour`. A device or a name: `hour` only.

parameters.name: kind

parameters.name: key

`queries` (default) or `blocked` (the network and names; a device's blocked queries
aren't kept per hour).

400.description: Invalid request: problem+json says which parameter and how to fix it.

422.description: `heatmap_window`: the window is too long for the grain, or a device or a name with a finer grain than hours; `privacy_level`: the privacy level hides names or devices.

Exemplars: for each answer path and latency bucket, a recent real query (at most one per
path and bucket a second; the last 512 per node are kept, in memory only), newest first,
at most 2,048. Each `traceId` opens the query in the log (`GET /api/v1/queries?trace=`), so
a dot on the latency heatmap leads to the query behind it. Every node's. Needs the
`querylog:read` scope for agents (a trace ID names a query).

get.description:
The latency histogram over time: for each minute (up to 48 hours) or hour (up to 400 days),
how many answers landed in each `wrendns_query_duration_seconds` bucket (`boundsUs`: 50 µs
to 5 s, then everything slower), per answer path (`by=path`: `cache`, `upstream`, `local`,
`synthesized` for blocked and special answers) or per upstream (`by=upstream`). Every node's,
summed. `partial` says some steps had answers without bucket counts (an older build's). Use
it to see a latency tail as a shape over time rather than a p99. Example:
`GET /api/v1/stats/latency/heatmap?from=-6h&by=path`.

Two objectives over every node's answers (`[slo]`): `availability`, the share of answers
that aren't SERVFAIL (default target 99.9%), and `latency`, the share sent within
`latency_ms` (default 99% within 250 ms). For each: the SLI and error budget left over
`window_days` (default 30), burn rates over 5m, 30m, 1h, 6h, and 3d (1 = spending exactly
the budget), and `alert`: `fast` (14.4× over 1h and 5m) or `slow` (6× over 6h and 30m)
degrade the health level and fire `slo_burn` alert rules; `ticket` (1× over 3d and 6h) is
shown only. Queries dropped without an answer count for neither. Example:
`GET /api/v1/stats/slo`.

objective's threshold), the window's bad answers broken down: `byClient` and `byName`
(approximate top lists, each row with `errorMax`: the true count is at least
`bad - errorMax`), and `byStatus` (`refreshed`, `forwarded`, ...), `byUpstream` (`none`: no
upstream on the answer, such as one served from the cache), `byRcode`, `byNode`, exact.
`timeline` is every node's bad answers per hour or day (`step`), with the share of the
window's budget each spent; `budget` the window's totals. In a cluster every node is asked;
`coverage.partialNodes` names nodes whose client and name lists are missing for part of the
window (they still count in the exact lists). Follows the query log's privacy level. Use it
to answer "why did the error budget drop?". Example:
`GET /api/v1/stats/slo/attribution?objective=availability&from=-30d`.

get.summary: How WrenDNS is doing: healthy, degraded, or severe, and why.
get.description:
`severe`: DNS is failing for some devices (every upstream of a group down, no node serving,
SERVFAIL for 25% or more of the last 5 minutes' queries). `degraded`: DNS answers, but
something needs a look (one upstream down, a cluster node unreachable or behind, a list
failing to download, devices rate-limited in the last 5 minutes, SERVFAIL for 5% or more, a
data disk over 90% full). Each reason names its node and where to look in the web UI. In a
cluster every node is asked; one that doesn't answer is listed in `missingNodes`. Each
condition is judged over its own window (the circuit breaker, the last 5 minutes, the
cluster heartbeat), so a brief blip doesn't change the level. Device anomalies don't count.

Version, role, uptime, listeners, whether the query log is on, and the active filter
snapshot. Cheap; suitable for health dashboards.

get.summary: Synthetic probes of the DNS listeners.
get.description:
Every `[probe] interval_secs` (30), each node asks each of its own DNS listeners a question
(`probe.wrendns.invalid`, answered NXDOMAIN locally) through the listener's protocol (UDP,
TCP, DoT, DoH, DoH3, DoQ), plus any extra `[probe] targets` (a load balancer's address). Per
probe: whether the last one answered, how long it took, the error, failures in a row, and for
TLS listeners the certificate's expiry. Two failures in a row, or a certificate within
`cert_warn_days`, degrade the health level (an expired one is severe). Every node, in a
cluster; one that doesn't answer is in `missingNodes`.

post.description:
One `.tar.gz` for an issue report: build and platform facts, the effective configuration
without secrets, the cluster view and timeline, health checks, upstream and listener state,
list names and counts (no domains), a metrics snapshot, aggregate statistics, and the node's
recent log lines, with a manifest that lists every file and counts what was removed or
replaced. Secrets (passwords and hashes, tokens, keys, credentials) are removed at every
level. Nothing is uploaded: the response is the archive.

**`level`** decides how much is obfuscated. `strict` (the default): addresses, MAC
addresses, host, device, group, node and pod names, e-mail addresses, URL hosts, and home
paths become pseudonyms that are stable inside the package and can't be reversed from it,
no query names, no free text, warnings and errors only in the log. `standard`: also INFO
log lines, top lists with pseudonymized names, and (with `querySample`) a query-log sample.
`none`: values as they are (secrets still removed). `reveal` keeps the named values readable.

With `keepMap`, the answer carries `X-Support-Package-Id`, and `GET
/system/support-package/{id}/map` returns the pseudonyms and the real values behind them once,
within ten minutes: it is not for attaching. `?dryRun=true` answers with the manifest only.

With **`cluster`**, the package covers every reachable node: each makes and redacts its own part
under one key made for this package (sent over the cluster channel, never stored), so a device
has the same pseudonym in every node's files and no real value crosses the network. The
manifest lists each node and whether it answered; the size cap is shared. Not with `keepMap`.
Free text is redacted by pattern, which is best effort: look the package over before you
attach it. Admin only; audit-logged as `support.package`. Not an MCP tool.

files define is read-only here (409 `set_by_file`), and so is its zone file (guarded, T27.17).
Needs the operator role (or the `config:write:records` agent scope, with a reason).

parameters.description: The zone's apex, e.g. home.example.com.

parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

parameters.description:

change would have done to those queries (`simulation`). `auto`: only when
`[simulate] plans_by_default` is on.

parameters.description:

The names it answered go back to the upstreams. A zone the configuration files define can't be
removed here (409).

404.description: Not found.
