ActiveDrill.description: REQ: CLU-014 — the drill running on a node.

dropped.description: Queries not answered so far, and from how many devices.

AffinityNode.description: REQ: CLU-014 — one node's share of a device's queries.

AffinityRow.description: REQ: CLU-014 — how a device's queries spread over the nodes.

label.description: `mostly <node>` (90 % or more on one node) or `both` / `several`.

topNode.description: The node it used most, and its share of the queries.

AgentCapability.description: REQ: DSC-004 (ADR-908 "Capability record") — what an agent answered when it was probed.

engineId.description: The v3 engine ID, in hex.

parts.description: One entry per part of every configured table.

sysObjectId.description: sysObjectID, when the agent answered it (device-supplied).

AgentCapabilityPart.description: REQ: DSC-004 — one part of a table group and the MIB table that answered it.

source.description:
The MIB table that answered (`ipNetToPhysicalTable`, `ipNetToMediaTable`, ...); none when
no alternative did.

AlertDelivery.description: REQ: OBS-010 (T9.6) — the last delivery to a destination.

AlertTest.description: REQ: OBS-010 (T9.6) — the result of a test alert.

error.description: Why it wasn't delivered (the destination's own message where there is one).

AlertsStatus.description: REQ: OBS-010 (T9.6) — alerts now: what fires, and how deliveries went.

evaluating.description:
Rules are checked on the cluster's primary (or a standalone node); elsewhere this is
false and the lists are empty.

maintenance.description: REQ: OPS-010 — nodes whose alerts are paused for maintenance, until when.

Annotation.description:
REQ: OBS-033 (ADR-133) — one change marker: something done to a node, or that it did to
itself, at a moment. The same shape is a line of `<data_dir>/annotations.jsonl`. Which
fields are set depends on `kind`.

actor.description:
Who, when known: a user, `token:<name> (owner: <user>)`, or
`agent:<name> (owner: <user>)`.

filterVersion.description: `config.applied` on a replica, `lists.refreshed`: the filter snapshot version.

href.description: Where the web UI shows more (`#/settings?tab=system`, `#/cluster`, `#/lists`).

lists.description: `lists.refreshed`: the lists whose content changed (added, removed, or downloaded anew).

node.description: The node it happened on (federated reads; a standalone node leaves it out).

nodes.description: `blocking.*`, `cache.flushed`: the nodes it was done on, when not only this one.

seq.description:
`config.applied`: the configuration sequence (the cluster's, else this node's
configuration version).

source.description:
`config.applied`: where the change came from: `ui` (a signed-in user), `api` (an API
token), `agent` (an agent token), `gitops`, `file` (the config files were reloaded),
or `cluster` (a replica applying the primary's version).

uncleanShutdown.description: `node.restarted`: the run before didn't stop cleanly (a crash, an OOM kill, a power cut).

AnnotationPage.description: REQ: OBS-033 — a page of change markers, newest first.

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read.

nextBefore.description: With `truncated`: the `before` for the next page (the oldest marker's time).

truncated.description: More markers in the window than `limit`: ask again with `before = nextBefore`.

AnomalyAckInfo.description: REQ: OBS-014 — an acknowledgement: someone looked at the finding.

note.description: Why (acknowledging only; at most 200 characters), shown with the finding.

AnomalyAckResult.description: REQ: OBS-014 — what an acknowledge or unacknowledge changed.

changed.description: Findings whose state changed (one already acknowledged doesn't count again).

unknown.description:
The IDs asked about that aren't current findings on any node that answered (still
recorded when acknowledging, in case a node that found them was unreachable).

AnomalyFinding.description: A device anomaly and its evidence (OBS-013). Alert-only: WrenDNS never acts on it.

oneOf.description: REQ: OBS-014 — who acknowledged it and when; absent while nobody has.

client.description: The device's address, and its name when known.

detail.description: The finding in words, with the numbers.

domain.description: The registrable domain, for domain findings.

id.description:
REQ: OBS-014 — stable ID (from the kind, device, domain, and window): the same finding
has the same ID on every node and after restarts. Acknowledge findings by it.

informational.description:
REQ: OBS-036 — a finding to see, not an anomaly (`chatty_loop`): left out of the sidebar
badge and the `anomaly` alert rule.

mutedBy.description:
REQ: OBS-038 (ADR-161) — the anomaly mute (its name) that matched this finding when it
was created. A muted finding is kept and listed, but not counted in
`wrendns_anomalies_total`, the sidebar badge, or the `anomaly` alert rule. Absent when no
mute matched; listed only with `muted=true`.

nodes.description:
REQ: OBS-014, CLU-002 — the cluster nodes that found it (each learns from the queries it
answers). Empty on a standalone node.

observed.description: What was seen, the device's usual value (± spread), and the bar it crossed.

rhythm.description:
REQ: OBS-031 — a beacon's (or a chatty loop's) rhythm when it was reported: 24 counts of
gaps between its queries per log-spaced bin (bounds in `GET /api/v1/clients/{id}/rhythm`'s
`binsS`).

windowStart.description: The window examined (RFC 3339 start, and length in seconds).

AttributionBudget.description: REQ: OBS-027 — the budget over the window.

allowedBad.description: Bad answers the target allows over the window.

answered.description: Answers counted (availability: every response; latency: every answer with a timing).

targetPct.description: The objective's target, percent of good answers.

AttributionCoverage.description: REQ: OBS-027 — how much of the window the lists cover.

approximate.description: The client and name lists are approximate (always).

hidden.description:
Why a list is empty on purpose: `names_hidden` (privacy level 1: names are hashes),
`clients_hidden` (level 2), `timeline_only` (level 3).

partialNodes.description:
Nodes without client and name lists for some of the window (an older build; a resolver
pod counted from the minutes it shipped): their bad answers count everywhere else.

topListsFromHours.description: Hours whose client and name lists were found (summed over nodes).

AttributionPoint.description: REQ: OBS-027 — one node's bad answers in one hour or day.

budgetSpentPct.description: The window's budget this spent, percent.

AttributionRow.description: REQ: OBS-027 — one row of a breakdown.

exact.description:
Exact count (`false` for the client and name lists: their `bad` is an upper bound, and
the true count is at least `bad - errorMax`).

key.description:
A client address, a name, a status, an upstream (`none`: no upstream on the answer),
a response code, or a node.

name.description: A client's device name, when it has one.

sharePct.description: Of the window's bad answers, percent.

actor.description:
A username, `token:<name> (owner: <user>)`, or a system name (`setup-token`,
`bootstrap`, `lockout`, `reload`).

detail.description: Details (what changed, as `{field: {from, to}}` for updates). Never secrets.

hash.description: BLAKE3 of the previous entry's hash and this entry (hex).

AuditPage.description: A page of the audit log, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for older entries; absent at the start of the log.

AuditVerify.description: Result of checking the hash chain.

firstBadSeq.description: The first entry that was changed, removed, or reordered.

headHash.description: Hash of the newest entry (hex). Record it elsewhere to detect truncation later.

ok.description: Every entry's hash and link checks out.

AuthStatus.description: Whether setup is needed and who is signed in (public).

csrfToken.description: For session sign-ins: send as `X-CSRF-Token` on changes.

localLogin.description:
Password sign-in is offered to this client (off with `disable_local_login`, except
from the break-glass admin networks).

oidc.description: OIDC providers: send the browser to `GET /api/v1/auth/oidc/{id}/start`.

setupRequired.description: No user exists yet: create the first admin with the setup token.

BackupRequest.description: REQ: API-007 (T23.9, ADR-903 §8) — the body of `POST /api/v1/backup`.

includeQlog.description: Also include the query log (refused when it is too big to build in memory: use the CLI).

passphrase.description:
At least 12 characters. With one, the node's stored secrets are encrypted into the backup
(`data/secrets.enc`, Argon2id and ChaCha20-Poly1305), and the request needs a session
signed in within the last 10 minutes. Write-only: never answered, logged or audited.

blocking.description: `true` ends every pause, `false` pauses blocking for everyone.

timer.description:
Seconds to stay off (rounded up to whole minutes; none: the longest allowed). Anything but
a number counts as none: the Home Assistant integration sends `true` for "no timer".

error.description: Set when the node couldn't be reached.

node.description: The node (absent on a standalone node).

pauses.description: Active pauses; empty: blocking is on.

BlockingRequest.description: REQ: FLT-009 (T7.1) — pause or resume blocking (`POST /api/v1/blocking/pause|resume`).

group.description: One group's devices only; absent: everyone (resume: every pause).

minutes.description: Pause only: for how long, 1 to 1,440 (agents: at most 60).

node.description: One node only (its site, pod, or ID); absent: every node.

added.description: Sources the proposal adds that no group had selected.

group.description: The group the proposal is for, when there is one.

heavyAdded.description: Heavy sources among `added`: they ask for a confirmation that states the daily download.

heavyDailyDownloadBytes.description: The daily download of `heavyAdded`, in bytes.

total.description: All groups' sources together, with the proposal in place.

BuildInfo.description: The build identity (REQ: OPS-004, ADR-046): the same on every architecture of one commit.

version.description: `0.1.0` (release), `0.1.0-edge.47` (main build), or `0.1.0-dev` (local build, read by peers as 0.1.0).

CacheEntry.description: One cached answer for a name.

checkingDisabled.description: The variant for clients that set CD (checking disabled).

dnssecOk.description: The variant for clients that set DO (they get DNSSEC records).

node.description: The node holding it (absent on a standalone node).

ttlLeftSeconds.description: Seconds until it goes stale; negative: how long it has been stale.

recursorRemoved.description:
REQ: DNS-905 (T40.4) — recursor entries dropped (a `recursor` flush): zone cuts and
addresses, or server round-trip times.

removed.description: Entries removed; absent when the node couldn't be reached.

node.description: One node only (its site or ID); absent: every node.

recursor.description:
REQ: DNS-905 (T40.4) — instead of answers, empty what the recursive resolver
remembers: `cuts` (zone cuts and server addresses: the next lookup starts from the
root), `rtts` (each server's round-trip time), or `all`. Can't be combined with
`name`, `subtree`, `type` or `kind`.

type.description:
REQ: DNS-905 (T40.4) — only this query type (`A`, `AAAA`, `HTTPS`, `TYPE65`): with a
`name`, that name's answers of this type; without, every name's.

CacheLookup.description: What the cache holds for a name.

CacheMakeup.description: REQ: DNS-006, OBS-003 (T6.15) — what the cache holds by kind (entries).

nodata.description: The name exists, but not with that type.

stale.description: Expired, kept only to serve stale when upstreams fail.

CacheNodeEntries.description: One node's top entries and makeup (`GET /api/v1/cache/entries`).

error.description: Set when the node couldn't be asked.

node.description: The node (absent on a standalone node).

CacheNodeStats.description: REQ: DNS-006 (T6.13) — one node's cache counters.

answeredPercent.description:
REQ: DNS-007 — lookups answered from the cache, fresh or from an expired entry
(refreshed in the background, or stale), percent: what the dashboard's cache tile shows.
Absent before any lookup, and from older nodes.

history.description: The last hour, every 15 s, oldest first (empty from older nodes).

hitPercent.description: hits / (hits + misses), percent; absent before any lookup. Fresh entries only.

node.description: The node (its site), or absent for a standalone node.

REQ: DNS-006, OBS-003 (T6.15) — the `[cache]` settings in effect (absent from older
nodes).

Whether the cache was reloaded from its dump at the last start (DNS-009).

CachePoint.description: REQ: OBS-003 (T6.15) — 15 s of one node's cache.

answeredPercent.description:
REQ: DNS-007 — lookups answered from the cache (fresh, refreshed, or stale) in the
interval, percent; absent without lookups, and from older nodes.

entries.description: At the end of the interval.

hitPercent.description: Hits per lookup in the interval, percent; absent without lookups.

CacheSettings.description: REQ: DNS-006 (T6.15) — the `[cache]` settings a node runs with.

maxEntries.description: Entry cap; absent: limited by memory only.

negativeTtlMaxSeconds.description: Cap for negative answers (NXDOMAIN, no data), RFC 2308.

prefetchMinHits.description: ...for answers asked at least this often.

prefetchThresholdPercent.description: Prefetch below this share of the TTL left.

serveStale.description: Serve expired answers when upstreams fail (RFC 8767).

servfailTtlSeconds.description: How long SERVFAIL is cached, RFC 9520.

REQ: DNS-007 — how long an expired answer waits for the upstream before it's given
(`[cache] stale_answer_client_timeout_ms`): 0 answers at once and refreshes in the
background. Absent from older nodes.

staleMaxAgeSeconds.description: How long expired answers are kept for that.

ttlLeftSeconds.description: Seconds until it goes stale; negative: how long it has been stale.

loaded.description: Answers reloaded; absent when nothing was loaded.

note.description: Why nothing was loaded (no dump, a dump from other upstreams, ...).

attributions.description: The attribution lines to show (CC BY-SA sources).

total.description: What all of them cost together (distinct sources).

What the node knows that bounds a selection (read from the primary in a cluster: it fetches
and compiles, ADR-994 item 10).

compileMemoryBytes.description: `[filter] compile_memory`, the merge budget before it is scaled to the node.

memoryLimitBytes.description: The node's memory limit (its cgroup, else its RAM), when known.

node.description: Which node these numbers are from.

processRssBytes.description: This process's resident memory now, when known.

CategoryGroupView.description: A group of categories in the picker.

note.description: A notice for the group's heading (an aggregate of other maintainers' lists says so).

noteUrl.description: The page the notice points to.

description.description: One line for the info icon.

entries.description: Entries with the default tier (distinct sources).

heavy.description: Any source it can use is heavy.

services.description: For a service category: the FLT-012 service IDs to put in `blockedServices`.

tierFrom.description: `adsTier`: the size is the `[filter] ads_tier` setting, not a per-profile choice.

warn.description: A warning the confirmation repeats (a category that blocks whole top-level domains).

CheckResult.description: REQ: API-002 (T9.12) — a pre-save check of a draft upstream or list.

detail.description: What was seen: `answered NOERROR, 13 records` or `81,234 rules from 81,512 lines`.

elapsedMs.description: How long the probe or the download took.

error.description: Why not (the server's or the parser's own message where there is one).

ok.description: It works: the upstream answered, or the list downloaded and has rules.

warnings.description: Lists: up to 10 lines that were invalid or unsupported, with why.

ClientChange.description: What a device change did, or would do with `dryRun=true` (AGT-002).

oneOf.description: The device after the change (absent after a delete).
The device before the change (absent when it's new).

configVersion.description: The configuration version after the change (send it as `If-Match` next time).

impact.description: What the change does, in one sentence, with the numbers (AGT-002 impact estimate).

recentQueries.description:
Queries in the current and previous hour from the addresses it matches: how much
history gets the new label (names are resolved when read, so the past is relabelled).

oneOf.description:
REQ: OBS-024 (T13.1) — with `simulate=` on a dry run: what the change would have done
to the queries in the query log.

effectiveGroups.description:
The groups that actually apply, highest priority first: `groups` when set, else the
group of the network its addresses are in (ADR-050), else the default group. Empty
when it depends on the address it's seen at (a device known only by MAC).

oneOf.description:
REQ: OBS-025 — what it looks like (the identity of the first of its addresses that was
seen), without the evidence (`GET /api/v1/clients/{id}/identity` has it).

kind.description: REQ: OBS-025 — what kind of device it is, as set (`[[client]] kind`), if set.

match.description: IPs, CIDRs, MACs, or `id:<client-id>` this device is recognized by.

source.description:
`file` (defined in the config files: read-only here) or `api` (named in the UI or
through the API: editable with `PUT /clients/{name}`).

ClientInput.description: A device to create, rename, or change (`PUT /api/v1/clients/{name}`, API-010).

kind.description:
REQ: OBS-025 — what kind of device it is (`camera`, `tv`, `unknown` to stop guessing);
wins over identification.

match.description: How to recognize it: IPs, CIDRs, MACs (`aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff`), or `id:<client-id>`.

name.description: The new name, to rename the device (default: the name in the path).

ClientPolicy.description: REQ: FLT-006, API-010 (T24.30) — a device's effective policy.

address.description: The address the policy was resolved for.

atUnixSeconds.description: When it was read (Unix seconds); schedules and rule expiry are as of then.

client.description: What was asked for: a device's name, an address, or a workload.

device.description: The configured device it is (a `[[client]]`'s name, or the workload's).

groupKey.description: The network or router name that gave the group, when it isn't the device's own.

groups.description: Every group it is in, the first one's settings applying (the same as Explain's).

identifiedBy.description: How it was recognized: the same word Explain's `client.identifiedBy` says.

matchedKey.description: The key that matched, written as a `[[client]] match` is. Absent for `default`.

node.description: The node whose configuration answered (a replica asks the primary).

notes.description: Caveats: the address was a stand-in, another device wins, no filter snapshot yet.

precedence.description: The ladder a device is matched down, with the rung that decided.

ClientRhythm.description: REQ: OBS-031 — a device's rhythm per domain.

available.description: False when the anomaly engine is off (`reason: disabled`).

binsS.description: The bins' upper bounds in seconds; the last bin (7,290 s and longer) has none.

domains.description: Sorted by the dominant share, most regular first; at most 16.

ClientStatusCounts.description: A top-list client's queries by how they were answered.

cached.description: From the cache, including stale and refreshed answers.

ClusterCheck.description: One health check with a plain-language fix when it fails.

fix.description: What to do about it (failing checks only).

id.description:
Stable ID: `peers_up`, `primary_present`, `in_sync`, `sync_errors`, `serving`, `certificate`,
`failover`, `voter_links` (a voter reached only some of the time, T24.38).

ClusterConflict.description:
A version an old primary published after a newer primary took over: never applied
anywhere; listed so the change can be re-made on the current primary.

changed.description: Settings that differ from the current primary's version (dotted paths).

detectedAt.description: When the newer primary's version arrived (RFC 3339).

ClusterEvent.description: A cluster event (joins, connections, published and applied versions, failures).

ClusterFailover.description: Automatic failover as this node sees it (ADR-056).

active.description: Whether elections run: `auto`, with three or more voters, this node one of them.

leaseHeld.description: This node is the elected primary and its lease holds.

leaseSecondsLeft.description: How long its lease still runs, in seconds (primaries only).

reachableVoters.description: Voters this node has a stream to (itself included).

votedEpoch.description: The epoch and node this node last voted for.

ClusterInfo.description: This node's cluster membership and the peers it holds a stream with.

certExpiresAt.description: When this node's cluster certificate expires (RFC 3339).

configCreatedAt.description: When that version was created on the primary (RFC 3339).

configSeq.description: The configuration version this node published (primary) or applied (replica), CLU-003.

lastSyncFetched.description: Blobs fetched for the last applied version (replicas).

lastSyncMs.description: Fetch + apply time of the last sync, in milliseconds.

name.description: The name given at `wrendns cluster init`.

nodeId.description: This node's ID (from its key; stable across restarts).

peers.description: Peers this node has heard from since it started.

primary.description: Whether this node holds the cluster CA (the first node, until promotion arrives).

syncError.description: The last replication error, until the next success.

behindSeconds.description: How long it has been behind (absent when in sync).

cacheEntries.description:
Its cache: entries, and over the last minute the cache share of its answers that weren't
blocked or local, as on the dashboard (absent without any).

certExpiresAt.description: This node only: when its cluster certificate expires (RFC 3339).

configSource.description: How the node's own configuration is managed: `gitops` or `file` (ADR-048).

connected.description: A stream to it is open (this node: n/a, true).

ephemeral.description: A Kubernetes resolver pod (CLU-009): dropped when no longer heard from.

oneOf.description: The machine it runs on (T6.11); absent from older nodes and before the first sample.

kubeNode.description:
REQ: CLU-008 (T6.14) — the Kubernetes node and pod it runs in (absent elsewhere and
from older nodes).

link.description:
`self`, `inbound` (it connected to this node), `outbound`, or `relayed` (no stream: a
peer reports it up, as the primary does for a replica in manual failover).

oneOf.description:
REQ: OPS-010 — its maintenance window, while it's in maintenance (older nodes never
report one).

primarySilentSeconds.description:
REQ: OBS-010 (T24.5, fork #2) — a replica's time without reaching its primary, in seconds
(the `primary_unreachable` alert and the health icon read it). Absent when it reaches the
primary, is the primary, or isn't heard from.

protocol.description: The cluster protocol it speaks (CLU-010); nodes within one version work together.

qps.description:
Queries per second over the last minute, to two decimals (a node one minor version older
reports whole numbers).

querySharePercent.description:
Its share of the queries the nodes that are up answered over the last minute, percent
(absent when there were none).

ready.description: Serving DNS (listeners bound, not shutting down).

restarts.description: Restarts this node has seen since it started itself (0 for this node).

rttMs.description: Round-trip time over the cluster link.

oneOf.description:
REQ: CLU-015 (ADR-903 §6) — its stored secrets: stamps and counts, never a value. Absent
from older nodes and from nodes not heard from.

servfailPercent.description: SERVFAIL share over the last minute, percent.

sourceCommit.description: The Git commit of the configuration it serves (ADR-049).

startedAt.description: When its process started (RFC 3339); absent from older nodes.

up.description:
Heard from within 15 s (always true for this node), by this node or, for a member it has
no stream to, by a peer that says so (`link` `relayed`).

oneOf.description: REQ: CLU-009 (T24.33) — for a witness: its vote state (absent for other nodes).

witness.description:
Votes in automatic failover only (ADR-056). A witness has no configuration version, no
secrets and no DNS: `configSeq`, `configLag`, `secrets` and `ready` mean nothing for it
(REQ: CLU-009, T24.33, ADR-1011), and the checks and alerts about them skip it.

configSeq.description: The configuration version the peer reports as applied (the primary: published).

up.description: Heard from within the last three heartbeats (15 s).

ClusterPin.description: REQ: CLU-013 — what pins the cluster.

by.description: Who pinned it: a user, `<user> via <node>`, or `the guard`.

changes.description: The same, one sentence per section (`list: changed`).

diff.description:
What the pin holds back: JSON Patch operations from the pinned version's shared
configuration to the one the primary would publish once unpinned (the primary only).

to.description: The version whose content every node serves, `epoch.seq`.

ClusterRollout.description: REQ: CLU-013 — the staged rollout and the pin, as the cluster view shows them.

canaries.description: The canary nodes it went to.

canariesOfflineSeconds.description:
How long canaries have been set with none online (seconds): changes reach every node at
once meanwhile.

oneOf.description: The last version the guard failed.

ClusterSecrets.description:
REQ: CLU-015 (ADR-903 §6) — one member's stored secrets. Stamps are `epoch.seq`; a value is
never here.

applied.description: The head it has applied from the primary (the primary's own, on the primary).

head.description: The newest stamp in its secrets head.

held.description: Secrets the primary holds but couldn't decrypt to send: this node keeps its own copy.

inSync.description: Its applied head is the primary's head: same stamps and digest.

unreadable.description: Live secrets it can't read here (encrypted under a key it doesn't have, or damaged).

ClusterSource.description: The cluster's configuration from Git (ADR-049): the commit in use and the last check.

checkedAt.description: When the primary last checked the ref (RFC 3339; on the primary only).

commit.description: The commit every node should be serving.

error.description: Why the last check failed, or why the newest commit was refused.

refused.description:
The newest commit isn't acceptable (invalid, unsigned, rewound): the cluster stays on
`commit`.

signedBy.description: The allowed signer who signed it (with `require_signed`).

by.description: What made it: this node's configuration, a Git commit.

current.description: Every node runs it (or is getting it) now.

pinnable.description: Its files are all kept, so the cluster can be pinned to it.

pinnedTo.description: For a pin: the version whose content it serves, and why.

ClusterView.description:
The cluster as this node sees it (REQ: CLU-008): every node with its health, sync, and
serving state, a timeline, and a pass/fail check list.

authority.description: Where the cluster's configuration comes from: `api` or `gitops` (ADR-048).

conflicts.description: Versions this node published that the cluster moved on without (ADR-051), newest first.

enabled.description: False on a standalone node (everything else is then empty).

oneOf.description: How the cluster fails over (ADR-056).
A standalone node's own machine (T6.11); in a cluster, each node carries its own.

newestConfigSeq.description: The newest configuration version any node reports.

nodes.description: This node first, then peers by site and ID.

oneOf.description:
REQ: CLU-013 — the staged rollout and the pin, in brief (`GET /cluster/rollout` has the
detail).
The Git repository the configuration comes from, when it does (ADR-049).

ClusterVote.description:
REQ: CLU-009 (T24.33, ADR-1011) — a witness's part in the election, as this node sees it. A
witness only votes: it has no configuration, no secrets and no DNS.

lastGrantSecondsAgo.description: Seconds since it last granted one.

lastReplySecondsAgo.description:
Seconds since it last answered a vote request or lease renewal from this node (absent: this
node hasn't asked it, as in manual failover or on a node that isn't the primary).

votedEpoch.description: The epoch it reported in its last reply (the epoch it voted in).

CmdbAlias.description: A merged-away id that redirects for 90 days.

CmdbChange.description: What a link, unlink, merge or split would do, or did.

notes.description: What else follows: an alias that redirects, a pin that is written.

result.description:
The device the records went to when it is new (a split or an unlink), or the one that
stayed (a merge).

daysSeen.description: Distinct days a presence source saw it, at most 32.

firstSeen.description: When the CMDB first saw it (Unix seconds).

id.description: `ci_` and 32 hex digits, random and never reused.

lastSeen.description: The newest time a presence source saw it, when known.

name.description: The name shown. Device-supplied text (cut and cleaned).

parent.description: For an interface: the device it belongs to.

proposals.description: Open merge proposals that name it.

records.description: How many source records are linked to it.

sources.description: The source kinds that report it.

unconfirmed.description: No source confirms it yet (a query-only or import-only record).

unmappedPort.description: A port that no alias joins to another source's port.

CmdbCiDetail.description:
`GET /api/v1/cmdb/cis/{id}`: a CI with its interfaces, its records side by side and what
reconciliation decided.

aliases.description: Ids merged into this CI that still redirect.

interfaces.description: The interfaces and ports under a device.

next.description: Pass this as `after` for the next page; absent on the last.

CmdbCount.description: A count of CIs of one type.

CmdbDropped.description: What the CMDB dropped at a cap (`wrendns_cmdb_dropped_total`).

batch.description: Batches the sink dropped because it was full.

ci.description: New CIs refused because every CI left is authored (at the cap).

record.description: New records dropped at the record caps.

CmdbLinkRequest.description:
Body of `POST /api/v1/cmdb/cis/{id}/link`: put a record (its interface, when it has a MAC) under
the device in the path.

CmdbMergeRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/v1/cmdb/cis/{id}/merge`: fold the device in the path into another.

into.description: The device that stays; the one in the path becomes an alias of it for 90 days.

from.description: The device it is on now.

to.description: The device it goes to; absent for a new device.

why.description: `its interface` (a MAC identifies an interface, so all its records go), `chosen` or `device`.

CmdbPin.description: A manual decision pinned to a CI.

CmdbProposal.description: A merge proposal: raised, never applied (ADR-1004 section 4).

rule.description: The rule that raised it: `R3`, `R4`, `R5` or `addr`.

CmdbRecord.description: One source record, as the source reported it.

attrs.description: The attributes as reported: device-supplied text, untrusted.

interface.description: The interface and the device it is linked to.

key.description: The thing's identity in that source.

state.description: `present`, or `absent` after two missed complete batches.

CmdbRecordRef.description: A record by its source and key.

key.description: The record's key in that source.

source.description: The source instance, as `GET /api/v1/cmdb/cis/{id}` shows it.

complete.description: Whether the batch listed everything the instance reports.

held.description: Records it holds in the database.

lastBatchUnix.description: When its last batch was ingested (Unix seconds).

source.description: The source instance (`unifi:home`, `snmp:core`, `neighbor`, ...).

CmdbSplitRequest.description:
Body of `POST /api/v1/cmdb/cis/{id}/split`: move chosen records of the device in the path to a
new device.

CmdbStatus.description:
`GET /api/v1/cmdb/status`: whether the CMDB runs on this node, what it holds, and what it
dropped. Health reasons never mark DNS unhealthy.

designated.description: Whether this node is the designated one (the node `[discovery]` designates).

diskBytes.description: The database and its WAL on disk, in bytes.

dropped.description: What was dropped at a cap.

headEpoch.description: The newest authored-row stamp: what a standby copies.

indexBytes.description: The in-memory index, an estimate in bytes.

lastError.description: The last error the CMDB logged, when it had one (it never touches DNS).

learningUntil.description: The end of the 24 h learning period (Unix seconds), while it runs.

node.description: The designated node's name, when `[discovery] node` names one.

proposalsOpen.description: Merge proposals waiting for a person.

running.description: Whether the CMDB's thread runs here.

sources.description: The last batch of each source instance.

CmdbUnlinkRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/v1/cmdb/cis/{id}/unlink`: take a record away from the device in the path.

ConfigChange.description: What a change to local names or forwarded domains did (or would do, with `dryRun`).

after.description: The entry after (absent after a delete).

configVersion.description: The configuration version after the change (send it as `If-Match` next time).

impact.description: What the change does, in one sentence, with the numbers (AGT-002 impact estimate).

keepInGit.description:
REQ: API-002 (T7.5, ADR-069) — on a node whose configuration comes from Git: the TOML
to add to (or the block to remove from) the repository or the Helm values' `config:` to
make this change permanent there. Changes made through the API live in this node's
`state.db`, not in Git. Absent on other nodes.

recentQueries.description:
Queries in the current and previous hour for the name (or names under the domain)
that the change affects. A lower bound: counted from the busiest names.

oneOf.description:
REQ: OBS-024 (T13.1) — with `simulate=` on a dry run: what the change would have done to
the queries in the query log. Absent otherwise.

ConfigEntry.description:
REQ: API-002 (T7.5, ADR-069) — one upstream, upstream group, list, or group: its definition
in effect and where it comes from.

answering.description:
REQ: DNS-023 (T24.13) — how many names this entry answers right now (the device names
for `local`).

credentialIssues.description:
REQ: API-014 (T23.2, ADR-903 §4) — paths this entry sets through the UI or API that the
path rules refuse (under `/proc` or the data directory, a key file, a credential file
outside `[node] secret_file_dirs`): they aren't read until an admin sets another.

definition.description:
The definition in effect, with the same fields as in `wrendns.toml` (absent when
hidden). Credentials read `<redacted>` (API-014).

redacted.description:
REQ: API-014 — the fields of `definition` that hold a credential and read `<redacted>`
(`headers.Authorization`, `args[1]`, `url` for a URL's password). Send them back as they
are to keep the values.

setByFile.description:
REQ: DNS-019, DNS-023 (ADR-914) — the fields of a shared settings section (`special`,
`local`, `clients`) that the config files set: the API can't change them, and the UI
shows them as "set by file".

source.description:
`file` (the config files), `added` (made through the UI or API), `override` (replaces
the files' entry of that name), or `hidden` (the files' entry is left out).

ContentInput.description: What to change in a group's content: fields left out keep their current value.

categories.description: Category IDs (`GET /api/v1/categories`); replaces the current list.

tiers.description: A tier per category (`gambling` = `extended`); replaces the current tiers.

expiresInDays.description: Ends after this many days (default: when revoked).

networks.description: Only from these addresses or networks (`10.20.2.0/24`, `10.0.0.5`); at most 16.

group.description: Agent tokens: only this client group's devices and queries.

oneOf.description:
`user` (default) or `agent`: an AI agent or automation, limited to `scopes`, rate
limited, attributed as `agent:<name>` in the audit log, and switched off with
`[agents] enabled = false`.

ratePerMinute.description: Agent tokens: requests per minute (default: `[agents] rate_per_minute`, 120).

oneOf.description: User tokens. Default: `read`.

scopes.description:
Agent tokens: any of `analytics:read`, `querylog:read`, `config:read`,
`config:write:clients`, `config:write:records`, `config:write:forwards`
(`config:write:*` for all three), `ops:pause`, `ops:cache`, `ops:anomalies`,
`cluster:admin`.
Default: `analytics:read` and `config:read` (read-only, no query log). Each needs a
role you have.

allowBasicApi.description: Allow HTTP Basic on the API for scripts and scrapers (default false).

CredentialField.description: A credential field of a node's configuration, with where its value comes from.

at.description: The file's path, or the stored secret's name (never a value).

node.description: The node this is about.

readable.description:
This node can read it (a file is opened without being read; a stored secret is judged by
its row, not decrypted).

source.description: `inline` or `file` (set by the configuration files: the UI won't edit it), or `stored`.

CredentialIssue.description: REQ: API-014 (T23.2) — a stored path that isn't read, and why.

DeviceIdentity.description:
REQ: OBS-025 (T13.3, ADR-117) — what a device looks like: a guess from its MAC vendor,
the names it announces, and the domains it talks to, or what it was set to be.

available.description: False when identification is off or not allowed (`reason`).

changedAt.description:
REQ: OBS-034 (T14.12) — when its product or class last changed (RFC 3339), and what it
looked like before (`Roku player`, or a class such as `unknown`).

client.description: The device's address (or client ID), as the query log shows it.

oneOf.description: Why (only from `GET /api/v1/clients/{id}/identity`).

node.description: The node that worked it out (in a cluster).

product.description: The product (`Roku player`), when it's at least `possibly`.

reason.description: `disabled`, `privacy_level`, or `not_seen` (no queries from it in the last day).

source.description: `inferred`, `override` (`[[client]] kind`), or `kubernetes` (a workload, FLT-017).

suggestedGroup.description: The group whose `device_classes` lists this class, when the device isn't in it.

DeviceTimeline.description: REQ: OBS-034 — one device's window as lanes and events.

coverageFrom.description: The query log keeps nothing older than this (RFC 3339), when it's inside the window.

markers.description: The change markers in the window (OBS-033), oldest first.

queries.description: Every query per bin, and the p99 answer time per bin (ms; null without queries).

source.description: `querylog`.

truncated.description: A read stopped early (rows, groups, or time): the lanes cover what it read.

DhcpLease.description: A device named by a router's DHCP or by mDNS (REQ: API-010; T8.2, T8.3).

clientName.description: The device's name in WrenDNS (a named client, else the host name).

dnsName.description:
REQ: DNS-023 (T22.1) — the name it answers as in DNS (`kitchen-tablet.home.arpa`),
with `[local] device_domain` set.

expiresUnixSeconds.description: When the router's lease ends (Unix seconds; 0 when unknown).

hostname.description: The name the router knows it by (its DHCP host name or alias), or the one it announces.

ipv6.description:
REQ: DNS-023 (T24.8, ADR-983) — the IPv6 addresses the router reports for the device
(global and unique-local, never link-local), up to 4. With `[local] device_domain` set,
each answers AAAA and an `ip6.arpa` PTR under `dnsName`.

offline.description:
REQ: T8.2 (ADR-166, ADR-942) — a client the router remembers but doesn't see now (UniFi's
offline clients). It is listed so the admin can see it, but it names no DNS name, gives
no discovery binding and isn't counted in a network's devices.

router.description:
REQ: API-012 (T22.3) — the `[[router]]` whose answer named it (`udm`,
`home-assistant`); absent for mDNS.

source.description:
`router` (read from a `[[router]]`) or `mdns` (the name the device announces,
`[clients] mdns`; no MAC).

DiscoveryAgent.description:
REQ: DSC-004, DSC-014 (T25.6, ADR-908) — one SNMP agent as the poller sees it. Everything that
came from the device (names, the sysObjectID) is device-supplied text, cut and cleaned.

address.description: The address it is polled at (RFC 1918 only).

oneOf.description:
What the agent answered when it was last probed (the first poll, or **Test**). Never
assumed: a table that did not answer is skipped until the next test.

consecutiveFailures.description: Polls that failed in a row.

credential.description: The credential it uses (by name; the secret is never shown).

oneOf.description: What the last poll's rows meant.

lastDurationMs.description: How long the last poll took, in milliseconds.

lastError.description: Why the last poll failed, in words. Carries no address, credential or reply byte.

lastPollUnix.description: When the last poll ended (Unix seconds).

lastRequests.description: SNMP requests the last poll sent.

lastSuccessUnix.description: When a poll last succeeded (Unix seconds).

lastTestUnix.description: When **Test** last ran for this agent (Unix seconds); a new test waits 60 s after it.

lastTimeouts.description: Exchanges of the last poll that timed out.

name.description: The agent's name, as `[[discovery.snmp_agent]]` gives it.

state.description:
`waiting` (no poll yet), `ok`, `error` (the last poll failed), `failing` (three polls in a
row failed) or `skipped` (its credential can't be read, or its address is refused).

DiscoveryAgentCounts.description: REQ: DSC-004, DSC-014 — what the last poll's rows meant.

arpMerged.description: ARP entries merged into the inventory.

arpOutsideSubnets.description: ARP entries outside every `[[discovery.subnet]]` (or naming no host).

fdbLocated.description: Forwarding entries that gave a device a port and a VLAN.

fdbUplink.description: Forwarding entries left out because they were learned on an uplink or trunk port.

ipv6Ignored.description: IPv6 entries counted and left out (M25 is IPv4 only).

uplinkPorts.description:
Ports counted as uplinks (more than 8 learned MACs, or a listed agent or UniFi device as
the LLDP neighbour).

DiscoveryAgentTable.description: REQ: DSC-004 — a configured table of an agent and what is known of it.

error.description: The last error of the table, in words.

rows.description: The rows the last poll read from the table, over every part and column.

stop.description: Why the last walk of the table ended: `end`, `row_cap`, `time_cap`, `byte_cap`, `error` or `skipped`.

DiscoveryRead.description:
REQ: DSC-009 (T25.10, ADR-912) - one extra read of one router, as the inventory thread last saw
it. Read-only: nothing here changes a console.

at.description: When the result was recorded (Unix seconds).

error.description: Why a read did not work, in words (no credential in it).

truncated.description: More rows were offered than the 8,192 cap; the rest were left out.

DiscoveryStatus.description:
REQ: DSC-014 (T25.3, ADR-908) — the network inventory's status: whether it runs on this node,
and each discovery worker process. Health reasons for the workers never mark DNS unhealthy.

agents.description:
REQ: DSC-004, DSC-014 (T25.6) — each `[[discovery.snmp_agent]]` the poller runs on this
node: its last poll, its tables and its capability record.

designated.description: Whether this node is the designated one (it runs the inventory and its workers).

node.description: The designated node's name, when `[discovery] node` is set.

reads.description:
REQ: DSC-009 (T25.10, ADR-912) - the last result of each extra UniFi and Home Assistant
read: which ones work, and which the console refused. Empty unless one is on.

workers.description: The worker processes this node runs (none unless enabled and designated).

DiscoveryWorker.description: REQ: DSC-002 (T25.3, ADR-908) — one discovery worker process, as the supervisor sees it.

dataLimitMib.description: The worker's `RLIMIT_DATA` in MiB, as it reported it at the handshake.

dumpable.description: Whether the worker reported it isn't dumpable (no core dumps, no /proc reads by others).

failing.description: Three or more crashes in ten minutes: restarts are slowed (`discovery_worker_failing`).

lastError.description: The last failure, in words (the stderr line is logged, rate-limited).

oomScoreAdj.description: The worker's `oom_score_adj`, as it reported it.

restarts.description: Times the worker has been restarted since start.

up.description: Running, with a handshake that matched.

versionMismatch.description: The worker's build differs from this node's: it is refused (`discovery_worker_version_mismatch`).

worker.description: `snmp` (the SNMP poller) or `import` (the scan-import parser, short-lived).

DisplayInfo.description: REQ: OBS-035 (T14.13) — a wall display token, as an admin sees it (never its secret).

networks.description: The addresses it may be used from (empty: anywhere).

DrillAll.description:
REQ: CLU-014 — `"all"`: every device (the node's infrastructure, cluster nodes, and
excluded devices are never dropped).

DrillCheck.description: REQ: CLU-014 — one precondition and whether it holds.

DrillDevice.description: REQ: CLU-014 — one device in a drill report.

client.description: Its address, or a Kubernetes workload's key.

dropped.description: Queries the drilled node didn't answer.

nodes.description: The nodes that answered it during the drill.

queriesElsewhere.description: Queries other nodes answered during the drill.

returned.description:
Whether it asked the drilled node again within 15 minutes after the drill (false:
it stayed on the other node, "sticky"); absent until checked, and for other verdicts.

timeToFailoverMs.description: First query elsewhere − first unanswered query (`followed` with something dropped).

verdict.description:
`followed` (asked another node after its first unanswered query, by 5 s after the end),
`stuck` (3 or more unanswered and no such answer: no working second server), `quiet`
(nothing unanswered, or too little: unknown), or `elsewhere` (not a target or in the
baseline; asked another node: informational).

DrillMode.description: REQ: CLU-014 (owner 2026-10-19) — what the drilled node does with its targets' queries.

DrillNodeCount.description: REQ: CLU-014 — queries one node answered (or dropped) during a drill.

balancerSwitchMs.description:
`viaBalancer`: last unanswered query − start (how long the balancer kept sending to the
not-ready pod).

baseline.description: Devices seen on the node in the hour before the drill.

devices.description:
Every device in the baseline, the targets, or seen anywhere during the drill (privacy
level 2 and above: empty, counts only).

nodes.description: Queries per node during the drill.

overflow.description: Devices not tracked because a table was full.

returnedChecked.description: Whether `returned` has been checked (15 minutes after the drill).

DrillReport.description: REQ: CLU-014 — a full drill report.

handover.description: On the primary under automatic failover: hand the role over first (default true).

oneOf.description:
`drop` (default: no answer at all, like a dead server) or `refused` (REFUSED at once:
faster, but some devices don't try their next server on it).

reason.description: Why, in a few words (1 to 200 characters, one line).
reason.example: does the Pi's second server work?

DrillStart.description: REQ: CLU-014 — a drill started (or, with `dryRun`, what would happen).

baseline.description: Devices seen on the node in the last hour (the report's baseline).

checks.description: Every precondition (on a start, all hold).

devices.description: On a dry run: the devices it would stop answering (at most 200).

handover.description:
As for maintenance: `started`, `unavailable` (the drill runs anyway: DNS is what's
tested), `declined`, `not_needed`, or `none`.

id.description: The drill's ID (empty on a dry run).

node.description: The node (its pod, site, or ID).

preview.description: In plain words, what it will do to devices.

since.description: When it started and ends (RFC 3339; on a dry run, as if now).

targetsResolved.description: Devices seen on the node in the last hour that the drill stops answering.

DrillSummary.description: REQ: CLU-014 — a drill in a list.

by.description: Who started it: a user, an agent, or `schedule` (`[drill] schedule`).

coveragePercent.description: followed / (followed + stuck), in percent; absent when neither.

ended.description: When it really ended (early with DELETE, or a restart).

missingNodes.description: Nodes whose part is missing (unreachable, or too old to record drills).

node.description: The drilled node.

status.description:
`running`, `collecting` (the 60-second grace and the other nodes' parts),
`complete`, or `cancelled` (a restart ended it; no report).

viaBalancer.description: A resolver pod behind one balancer address: the verdicts measure the balancer.

DrillTargetDevice.description: REQ: CLU-014 — a device a drill would stop answering (a dry run lists them).

DrillTargets.description:
REQ: CLU-014 — who a drill stops answering: `"all"`, `{ "clients": [...] }` (addresses,
device names, or Kubernetes workloads), or `{ "group": "iot" }`.

EdeCount.description: REQ: OBS-019 — answers carrying one EDE code.

category.description:
REQ: FLT-901 — the category (or categories) a `cat-` list stands for, for example "Adult
content"; absent for any other list.

device.description: The configured device it was recognized as.

group.description: The group whose settings apply (the first of `groups`).

groupKey.description: The network or router name that gave the group, when it isn't the device's own.

matchedKey.description:
REQ: FLT-006, API-010 (T24.30, ADR-996) — the key it matched on, written as a
`[[client]] match` is (`id:kids`, a MAC, an address, a network, `hostname:tv`), or the
workload's name. Absent for the `default` group.

oneOf.description: REQ: FLT-017 — the Kubernetes workload a pod address belongs to.

routed.description: An explicit route matched (not just the default group).

enabled.description: The client's groups use this list.

lines.description: Where the rule is in the list.

shadow.description:
REQ: OBS-018 — the list is in shadow mode: it never blocks, its would-be blocks are
counted.

ExplainWorkload.description: REQ: FLT-017 — a pod address's workload in an explanation.

Explanation.description: Why a name is or isn't blocked for a client, and where it would go (FLT-013).

oneOf.description: Every matching rule in precedence order; absent until a filter is loaded.

pausedUntilUnixSeconds.description: Blocking is paused for this client until then (Unix seconds).

oneOf.description: Where a forwarded query goes.

special.description:
REQ: DNS-019 (T24.12, ADR-914) — for `special`, the special-name rule that answered:
`private_relay`, `single_label`, `resolver_arpa`, `ddr`, `firefox_canary`, `private_ptr`,
`chaos`, or `localhost`. A rule's name, not a field of `[special]`: the UI maps it to the
switch that controls it.

FailureKinds.description: Failed attempts by kind (their sum is `failures`).

badResponse.description: An answer that didn't match the query or didn't parse.

network.description: A connection, TLS, or socket error.

servfail.description: The upstream answered SERVFAIL (often the domain's fault, not the upstream's).

timeout.description: No answer within the attempt's timeout.

unresolved.description: The upstream's hostname couldn't be resolved.

FiringAlert.description: REQ: OBS-010 (T9.6) — an alert that is firing now.

subject.description: What it's about: an upstream, a node, a list.

FlowLink.description: One link: answers counted for exactly this pair.

failure.description: Into a SERVFAIL (status or response code).

count.description: Answers through it (the larger of what comes in and what goes out).

deadEnd.description: Answers that end here (a dropped query has no response code).

ForwardInfo.description: A domain sent to other servers (conditional forwarding).

allowLocalServers.description: REQ: DNS-902 — a stub zone whose servers may be at loopback or link-local addresses.

allowPrivateServers.description:
REQ: DNS-902 — a stub zone whose private-range servers are also asked for names outside
the zone.

dnssecNta.description: REQ: DNS-010 (T27.7) — a DNSSEC negative trust anchor is added for the domain.

matchGroup.description: REQ: DNS-010 (T27.7) — the client groups the route applies to (empty: every client).

matchQtype.description: REQ: DNS-010 (T27.7) — the query types the route applies to (empty: all).

nodeOnly.description: REQ: CLU-006 (T27.7) — this route stays on this node.

servers.description: The servers (upstream URLs), in order; a stub zone's are IP addresses.

source.description: `file` (read-only here) or `api`.

stub.description:
REQ: DNS-022 — a stub zone: the servers are asked iteratively and their delegations
followed.

ForwardInput.description: The servers a domain is sent to (`PUT /api/v1/forwards/{domain}`).

allowLocalServers.description:
REQ: DNS-902 — a stub zone only: also ask its servers at loopback or link-local
addresses (a server on this machine). Off by default, and refused for a forward that
is not a stub zone. Left out, the stored value stays as it is.

allowPrivateServers.description:
REQ: DNS-902 — a stub zone only: also ask private-range servers for names outside the
zone (the zone's own private servers are asked either way). Off by default, and refused
for a forward that is not a stub zone. Left out, the stored value stays as it is.

dnssecNta.description:
REQ: DNS-010 (T27.7) — add a DNSSEC negative trust anchor for the domain (default `true`:
local zones are usually unsigned).

matchGroup.description: REQ: DNS-010 (T27.7) — only these client groups are sent (empty: every client).

matchQtype.description: REQ: DNS-010 (T27.7) — only these query types are sent, e.g. `["PTR"]` (empty: all).

nodeOnly.description: REQ: CLU-006 (T27.7) — keep this route on this node only.

servers.description:
Addresses (plain DNS) or `udp://`, `tcp://`, `tls://`, `https://` URLs, tried in order.
For a stub zone: the zone's own servers, as IP addresses (port 53).

stub.description:
REQ: DNS-022 — a stub zone (BIND's `static-stub`): the servers are authoritative only,
so they're asked iteratively and the delegations they give to other servers are
followed, instead of forwarding with recursion desired. Default `false`.

GeoipStatus.description:
REQ: OBS-902 (T26.4, ADR-959 section 6) - this node's GeoIP database: whether it is on, what
it holds, and how the last fetch went. Everyone who can see the map sees it.

attribution.description: The attribution the database's licence (CC BY 4.0) asks for.

lastError.description:
A stable code (`digest_mismatch`, `overlapping_ranges`, `not_found`, ...), never a
response body.

nextCheckAt.description: When the next check is due (a check runs at most once a day).

old.description: The database is more than 90 days old (it still works).

sourceMonth.description: The month of the database's source, `YYYY-MM`.

state.description:
`off`, `missing` (on, with no database on this node yet), `downloading`, `ready` or
`failed` (the last attempt was not accepted: `lastError` says why, and the previous
database, if any, is kept).

updatedAt.description: When this node built the database.

GroupContentInfo.description: A group's content as the API shows it.

categories.description: Category IDs (kept when the level is `off`).

level.description: `off`, `basic` or `enhanced`; left out reads `off`, as in the TOML.

GroupContentView.description: A group's content, and what it makes the node do.

blockedServices.description: REQ: FLT-012 (T7.9) — services this group blocks (IDs from `GET /api/v1/services`).

color.description: `#rrggbb` for charts and chips (configured, or a stable pick).

oneOf.description: REQ: FLT-902 (T24.29) — what the group filters by category (absent: nothing set).

devicesThisHour.description: Devices seen in the group this hour.

REQ: DNS-016 (T7.21) — AAAA answers synthesized for IPv4-only names (DNS64), and the
prefix (`64:ff9b::/96` unless set).

filterAaaa.description: REQ: FLT-016 (T12.5) — AAAA questions get no data (the group's devices use IPv4).

filterScope.description: REQ: FLT-902 — "Off", "Basic", "Enhanced (3 of 21)" and "Ad block", for the Filter Scope column.

lists.description: Lists this group uses; null means every enabled list.

networks.description: Networks (CIDRs) whose devices belong to this group (ADR-050).

pausedUntilUnixSeconds.description: Blocking is paused for this group until then (Unix seconds).

queries24h.description: Queries from the group's devices over the last 24 hours.

rebindingProtection.description:
REQ: FLT-014 (T7.20) — private addresses in public answers are blocked (DNS
rebinding protection), and the networks whose answers are filtered.

rewrites.description: REQ: FLT-015 (T7.20) — names answered with a fixed address or name.

safeSearch.description:
REQ: FLT-011 (T7.11) — safe search, and YouTube's restriction: `strict`, `moderate`,
or `off` (absent when safe search is off).

safeSearchEngines.description: REQ: FLT-902 — the engines safe search covers (empty with `safeSearch`: every engine).

schedules.description: REQ: FLT-010 (T7.10) — the group's schedules, and which of them are on now.

sources.description:
REQ: FLT-902 — who the group applies to: its networks, router names and devices, for the
profile list's Source column.

upstreams.description:
REQ: UPS-007 (T9.25) — the upstream group this group's queries go to (absent: `default`,
or wherever `[[route]]` entries send them).

categories.description: The categories in effect (the level's, plus ads), catalog order.

unknown.description: IDs this version does not know: ignored, and reported.

GuardReadings.description: REQ: CLU-013 — the guard's readings over a bake.

afterPercent.description: The same share during the bake.

answers.description:
Answers the canaries (and the primary) gave during the bake (the share is judged from
50 on).

beforePercent.description:
The canaries' (and the primary's) SERVFAIL share, in percent, over the bake before the
rollout began.

reason.description: Why the guard failed the version, when it did.

GuardedApplied.description: What happened to a request to change a guarded setting.

confirmToken.description:
`pending`: the single-use token that confirms it from the new address (put it in the
address's `#fragment`, never in a query).

deadlineSecs.description: `pending`: seconds left, on the node's monotonic clock.

message.description: What to tell the admin, in words.

newAddress.description: `pending`: where to confirm, when the confirmation has to arrive somewhere new.

pendingId.description: `pending`: the change waiting to be confirmed.

pendingRestart.description: `staged`: the change waits for the node's next start.

proof.description:
`pending`: what the confirming request has to prove (`new_socket`, `new_cert`,
`proxy_list`).

acknowledge.description: The extra acknowledgements the preview named.

confirm.description: The phrase the preview returned, typed by the admin. The server compares it.

node.description: The node the preview was for.

reason.description: Why: kept in the audit record.

value.description:
The same value (and options) the preview was made for: a different one is
409 `preview_stale`.

GuardedCheck.description: One check of a dry run.

confirmToken.description:
The single-use token the change answered with. Without one, the request must be the same
admin's session.

GuardedNodeStatus.description:
`GET /api/v1/guarded`: what is guarded on a node and what is pending. No value, preview ID or
confirmation token is ever in it.

confirmWindowSecs.description: The seconds a window change waits (`[api] confirm_window_secs`).

ignored.description:
`WRENDNS_IGNORE_GUARDED` is set: every guarded entry is ignored (health reason
`guarded_ignored`).

outcomes.description:
The latest outcomes (newest first, at most 10): applied, confirmed, or rolled back with
the reason.

oneOf.description: The window change waiting for confirmation, if any.

pendingRestart.description: Staged changes waiting for a restart (setting IDs).

restarting.description: A restart was accepted and the node is on its way down.

GuardedPending.description:
A window change waiting to be confirmed: what it is and how long is left, never its value, a
preview ID or the confirmation token.

deadlineSecs.description: Seconds left, measured on the node's monotonic clock.

id.description: The pending change's ID (what `confirm` and `cancel` name).

GuardedPendingView.description:
The answer of `GET /api/v1/guarded/pending/{id}`: the window's seconds left and, for a change that
binds DNS sockets, the node's own probe of each. It names the staged addresses, so it is for the
admin who made the change (the confirm token or that admin's session), unlike the status listing.

deadlineSecs.description: Seconds left, measured on the node's monotonic clock.

probes.description: One line per staged socket; empty for a change that has no probes.

GuardedPreview.description: The dry run's answer. Nothing was changed.

acknowledgements.description: A second acknowledgement the change needs (`acknowledgeNoAdmins`, ...), when it does.

effect.description: What the change does, in words.

needsRecentSignIn.description:
The change needs a session signed in within the last 10 minutes (it weakens security, or
it restarts the node).

previewId.description:
Send it back with the change. Bound to you, the node, the setting, the value and the
configuration version; lives 5 minutes.

proofPort.description: For a window change that needs a temporary parallel listener (a TLS-only change): its port.

setByFile.description: The setting is a file's: the control is locked.

weakening.description:
The change is weaker than what is set now: marked in red, and it needs a sign-in within
the last 10 minutes.

windowSecs.description: Seconds a window change would wait for its confirmation.

wouldDisconnect.description:
Once confirmed, the node would have no API or DNS listener, or this request's listener
would go.

node.description: The node the change is for (its ID or name). Default: the node answering.

options.description: Options the setting's form carries (for example `copyState`).

value.description:
The new value, in the shape the setting's configuration section has. Not needed for an
action such as `restart-now`.

GuardedProbeLine.description: One staged socket of a pending change, as `GET /api/v1/guarded/pending/{id}` shows it.

at.description: When the last probe finished (Unix seconds).

otherHosts.description:
Distinct other hosts whose queries reached this socket during the window (at most 64; IPv6
by /64; this node's own addresses left out). Shown, never required to confirm.

state.description:
`waiting` (no probe has finished yet), `answered`, `refused_by_gate` (the gate's own
refusal, the expected answer on a gated listener) or `no_answer`.

GuardedResult.description: The answer of a confirmation or a cancellation.

seenClient.description: For a `proxy_list` proof: the client address the node now sees for this request.

GuardedSetting.description: One guarded setting, as `GET /api/v1/guarded` lists it for this node.

hasEntry.description: A guarded entry holds a value for it (confirmed, applied or staged).

onProbation.description: A start has the entry on probation (it counts as applied once the node is healthy).

pendingRestart.description: A staged change waits for the node to restart.

setByFile.description: A file sets it, and wins: the control is locked and shows the file.

suppressed.description: A command-line clear is hiding the replicated entry until the primary's copy changes.

nodes.description: This node first, then the members the primary can see.

Health.description: REQ: OBS-015 (ADR-104) — how WrenDNS is doing, in one word, with the reasons.

level.description:
`healthy`, `degraded` (something needs a look, DNS answers), or `severe` (DNS is failing
or about to).

maintenance.description:
REQ: OPS-010 — nodes in maintenance: their conditions are left out of `reasons` and the
level until the window ends (a node in maintenance still answers DNS).

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that didn't answer (their own conditions aren't included).

reasons.description: Every condition found, the most serious first. Empty when healthy.

fromLabel.description:
REQ: API-013 (T35.3) — `from` and `to` in words (a device's name, an upstream's display
label), for an agent that reads the answer to a person.

HealthProblem.description: One node that isn't green, with why.

link.description: Where to look in the web UI (a `#/…` path).

node.description: The node it's about (cluster nodes only).

summary.example: upstream quad9 isn't answering (its circuit breaker is open)

covered.description:
A device or a name: false where the key wasn't in that hour's top list (its count is
then unknown, shown as "below this hour's top list"). Absent for the network.

starts.description: Each slot's start (Unix seconds, UTC), oldest first; parallel to `values`.

HostInfo.description: One host sample, with sizes in bytes and shares in percent.

cgroupCpuQuotaCores.description: The container's CPU quota, in cores.

cgroupMemLimitBytes.description: The container's (cgroup's) memory limit, when it has one.

clockOffsetMs.description: Its clock minus this node's, from heartbeats (peers only).

cpuPercent.description: Host CPU busy over the last 15 s.

diskTotalBytes.description: The filesystem holding the data directory.

oomKills.description: Processes killed for lack of memory in this container, ever.

sampledAt.description: When it was sampled (RFC 3339, the node's clock).

temperatureC.description: The hottest thermal zone (on a Pi, the system-on-chip).

throttledPercent.description: Share of the last 15 s the container was throttled by its quota.

warnings.description: What looks wrong, in plain words (low disk, memory pressure, heat, clock drift).

writeBytesPerSecond.description: What this process writes to storage (SD-card wear on a Pi).

HostPoint.description: A point of the last hour, for trend lines.

HostReport.description:
REQ: CLU-008 (T6.11) — the machine a node runs on: its latest sample, what looks wrong,
and the last hour. Values the node couldn't read are absent (see `unavailable`).

history.description: Up to an hour of samples (every 15 s), oldest first.

Hour.description: Which hour a top-K or latency call reads.

IdentityEvidence.description: REQ: OBS-025 — the evidence behind an identity.

domains.description: The signature's domains the device talked to, with their weights.

oneOf.description: REQ: FLT-017 — a Kubernetes workload: what the API server says (`source: kubernetes`).

matchedName.description: The announced name that matched the signature.

names.description: Every name the device announced (DHCP, mDNS).

oneOf.description: The next best guess, when it's within 0.1: "could also be …".

seenDomains.description: The registrable domains it talked to (at most 24).

Items_AnomalyFinding.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

items.description: A device anomaly and its evidence (OBS-013). Alert-only: WrenDNS never acts on it.

oneOf.description: REQ: OBS-014 — who acknowledged it and when; absent while nobody has.

client.description: The device's address, and its name when known.

detail.description: The finding in words, with the numbers.

domain.description: The registrable domain, for domain findings.

id.description:
REQ: OBS-014 — stable ID (from the kind, device, domain, and window): the same finding
has the same ID on every node and after restarts. Acknowledge findings by it.

informational.description:
REQ: OBS-036 — a finding to see, not an anomaly (`chatty_loop`): left out of the sidebar
badge and the `anomaly` alert rule.

mutedBy.description:
REQ: OBS-038 (ADR-161) — the anomaly mute (its name) that matched this finding when it
was created. A muted finding is kept and listed, but not counted in
`wrendns_anomalies_total`, the sidebar badge, or the `anomaly` alert rule. Absent when no
mute matched; listed only with `muted=true`.

nodes.description:
REQ: OBS-014, CLU-002 — the cluster nodes that found it (each learns from the queries it
answers). Empty on a standalone node.

observed.description: What was seen, the device's usual value (± spread), and the bar it crossed.

rhythm.description:
REQ: OBS-031 — a beacon's (or a chatty loop's) rhythm when it was reported: 24 counts of
gaps between its queries per log-spaced bin (bounds in `GET /api/v1/clients/{id}/rhythm`'s
`binsS`).

windowStart.description: The window examined (RFC 3339 start, and length in seconds).

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read, for federated reads (CLU-002).

Items_BlockingNode.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

items.description: One node's pauses (`GET /api/v1/blocking`).

error.description: Set when the node couldn't be reached.

node.description: The node (absent on a standalone node).

pauses.description: Active pauses; empty: blocking is on.

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read, for federated reads (CLU-002).

Items_CacheNodeEntries.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

items.description: One node's top entries and makeup (`GET /api/v1/cache/entries`).

error.description: Set when the node couldn't be asked.

node.description: The node (absent on a standalone node).

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read, for federated reads (CLU-002).

Items_CacheNodeStats.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

items.description: REQ: DNS-006 (T6.13) — one node's cache counters.

answeredPercent.description:
REQ: DNS-007 — lookups answered from the cache, fresh or from an expired entry
(refreshed in the background, or stale), percent: what the dashboard's cache tile shows.
Absent before any lookup, and from older nodes.

history.description: The last hour, every 15 s, oldest first (empty from older nodes).

hitPercent.description: hits / (hits + misses), percent; absent before any lookup. Fresh entries only.

node.description: The node (its site), or absent for a standalone node.

oneOf.description:
REQ: DNS-006, OBS-003 (T6.15) — the `[cache]` settings in effect (absent from older
nodes).
REQ: OBS-021 (T11.2) — whether the cache is the right size (absent from older nodes).
Whether the cache was reloaded from its dump at the last start (DNS-009).

group of the network its addresses are in (ADR-050), else the default group. Empty
when it depends on the address it's seen at (a device known only by MAC).

oneOf.description:
REQ: OBS-025 — what it looks like (the identity of the first of its addresses that was
seen), without the evidence (`GET /api/v1/clients/{id}/identity` has it).

kind.description: REQ: OBS-025 — what kind of device it is, as set (`[[client]] kind`), if set.

match.description: IPs, CIDRs, MACs, or `id:<client-id>` this device is recognized by.

source.description:
`file` (defined in the config files: read-only here) or `api` (named in the UI or
through the API: editable with `PUT /clients/{name}`).

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read, for federated reads (CLU-002).

REQ: API-002 (T7.5, ADR-069) — one upstream, upstream group, list, or group: its definition
in effect and where it comes from.

answering.description:
REQ: DNS-023 (T24.13) — how many names this entry answers right now (the device names
for `local`).

credentialIssues.description:

hidden). Credentials read `<redacted>` (API-014).

are to keep the values.

setByFile.description:

source.description:
`file` (the config files), `added` (made through the UI or API), `override` (replaces
the files' entry of that name), or `hidden` (the files' entry is left out).

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read, for federated reads (CLU-002).

the names it announces, and the domains it talks to, or what it was set to be.

available.description: False when identification is off or not allowed (`reason`).

source.description: `inferred`, `override` (`[[client]] kind`), or `kubernetes` (a workload, FLT-017).

suggestedGroup.description: The group whose `device_classes` lists this class, when the device isn't in it.

clientName.description: The device's name in WrenDNS (a named client, else the host name).

REQ: DNS-023 (T22.1) — the name it answers as in DNS (`kitchen-tablet.home.arpa`),

router.description:

`home-assistant`); absent for mDNS.

source.description:
`router` (read from a `[[router]]`) or `mdns` (the name the device announces,
`[clients] mdns`; no MAC).
