NodeAddress.description: One address this node holds, for the Upstreams form's `source` suggestions.

network.description: The network it is in, which a shared upstream can name instead: `198.51.100.0/24`.

NodeCompare.description: REQ: OBS-028 — every node side by side over one window.

missingNodes.description: Nodes that didn't answer; the findings cover the rest.

nodes.description:
This node first, then the others in the cluster view's order. Witnesses don't answer
DNS and aren't listed.

partial.description:
Some node had answers without latency counts (an older build's): its percentiles are
missing.

NodeFinding.description: A node that stands out on one metric, or a note on why it only looks like it does.

level.description:
`odd` (it deviates from the others) or `note` (it looks worse only because its base is
smaller). Never an error: this is a lens, not a condition.

oddSince.description:
When the deviation started (RFC 3339): the change point of the node's excess over the
others. Absent when it covers the whole window, or for latency.

others.description: The others' value: their median, or the other node's.

spread.description: The spread the deviation is measured against (1.4826 × MAD, floored).

NodeMaintenance.description:
REQ: OPS-010 (ADR-118) — a node's maintenance window: it reports not ready (balancers stop
sending it new queries), keeps answering, and is left out of alerts, the health level, and
elections until `until`.

by.description: Who started it: a user, `<user> via <site>` from another node, or an agent.

node.description: The node (its pod, site, or ID), in lists.

NodeNumbers.description: One node's numbers over the window.

fromCache.description: Answered from the cache (fresh, refreshed, or stale).

intervals.description: Wilson 95 % intervals of the percentages, `[low, high]`, by metric name.

label.description: Its pod name, else its site, else its ID.

p50Us.description: From the latency histograms (absent without any).

qps.description: Queries per second over the window.

NodeRemoval.description:
What removing a node from the cluster did, or with `dryRun` would do
(`DELETE /api/v1/cluster/nodes/{id}`, CLU-001, ADR-155).

automaticFailoverAfter.description: Whether automatic failover still runs (it needs three voters).

eligible.description: It could vote and be primary, so it holds a copy of the cluster key.

ephemeral.description: It was a Kubernetes resolver pod.

heldClusterKey.description:
Rotate the cluster CA if this node is lost or can't be trusted: removal stops the
cluster accepting it, but it keeps its copy of the key.

notes.description: What to do or expect next, one sentence each.

up.description: It was connected or heard from within the last few heartbeats.

NodeSection.description:
One per-node section: the fields in effect, which of them the files set, and whether a restart
is still pending for it.

fields.description: The fields in effect, with the same names as in `wrendns.toml`.

pendingRestart.description: The section differs from what the node started with: it applies after a restart.

restartOnly.description: Whether every field of the section applies only after a restart of the node.

setByFile.description: The fields the configuration files set: the API can't change them (409 `set_by_file`).

stored.description: Whether the API set this section for the node (`false`: the files' values apply).

NodeSeries.description:
One node's ratios over time, for the sparklines (at most 240 points: buckets summed into
spans). A span without a base (no answers, no upstream exchanges) is null.

NodeSettings.description:
REQ: DNS-006, OPS-011, OPS-012 (T27.2, T27.11, ADR-1006) — `GET /api/v1/node-settings/{node}`:
the per-node sections of one node (`cache`, `support`, `updates`).

node.description: The node the sections belong to.

NotOfferedView.description: A category the catalog does not offer, and why.

NoteRequest.description: REQ: OBS-033 — `POST /api/v1/annotations`: a note on every time chart.

text.example: moved the access point to the hallway

time.description: When it happened (RFC 3339; default now): up to 7 days back, never ahead.

OidcProviderEntry.description:
REQ: API-016 (T23.10, ADR-903 §6, ADR-967) — one OIDC provider as the API shows it: its
settings (the client secret as a name, never a value), where it comes from, and whether this
node serves its sign-in button.

active.description: Whether the button works on this node.

defaultRole.description: The role for people in no mapped group; absent means they can't sign in.

id.description: The short ID used in URLs.

reason.description:
Why it doesn't (no `public_url` on this node, an unreadable secret), or what went wrong
the last time the provider was read.

redirectUri.description: The address to register with the provider as the redirect URI; absent without `public_url`.

roles.description: Group to role rules, in order.

secret.description: The stored secret's name, when `secretSource` is `stored`.

secretReadable.description: Whether this node can read the secret now; absent when none is set.

secretSource.description:
Where the client secret comes from: `stored` (the encrypted store, by name), `file`,
`inline` (in the configuration file), or `none` (a public client).

source.description: `file` (the configuration files define it; read-only here) or `api`.

publicUrl.description:
This node's `[auth.oidc] public_url` (node-local, set in its file); empty when unset, and
then every provider is inactive here.

OidcRoleRuleInfo.description: One group to role rule of an OIDC provider.

code.description: The code from the display's link.

OtlpEntry.description: REQ: API-016, OBS-006 (T23.11) — `GET /api/v1/otlp`: the OTLP export in effect on this node.

active.description: Whether the export runs on this node.

endpoint.description: The collector's address (a password in it removed); absent when there is none.

reason.description: Why it doesn't, when an endpoint is set.

source.description:
`none` (no export), `file` (the configuration files set the destination; read-only here)
or `api`.

tracesSampleEvery.description: Trace settings (a file's; read at start).

OtlpHeader.description: REQ: API-016, OBS-006 (T23.11) — one header of the OTLP export.

readable.description: Whether this node can read the secret now (`stored` only).

secret.description: The stored secret's name, when `source` is `stored`.

source.description:
`stored` (a stored secret, by name) or `inline` (a value in the configuration file: never
shown, `<redacted>`; enter it as a stored secret to move it to the UI).

value.description: `<redacted>` for an inline value; absent for a stored one.

OverblockSuspect.description:
REQ: OBS-018 (ADR-109) — a blocked name that looks like it shouldn't be: devices kept
retrying it, or it was answered normally soon after being blocked (someone paused
blocking or allowed it).

allowedAfterBlock.description:
Times a device got it answered normally within 10 minutes of a block (a pause, a
quick allow, or an allowlist entry: someone wanted it).

devices.description: Devices involved (none counted at privacy level 2 and above).

name.description: Hashed at privacy level 1 and above.

retryBursts.description:
Times a device asked for it 10 or more times within a minute while it was blocked
(apps that break retry; ad libraries do too).

PiholeApiSettings.description: Body of `PUT /api/v1/pihole-api`: fields left out keep their value.

PiholeApiStatus.description: The settings as the admin API shows them: never the token.

enabled.description: Whether the Pi-hole compatible API answers. Off by default.

lastUsedUnixSeconds.description: When a request last carried the token (to the minute).

maxPauseMinutes.description:
The longest pause it may start, in minutes (1 to 1,440). Pi-hole's "disable with no timer"
pauses for this long.

tokenSet.description: Whether a token has been issued (the token itself is shown only when it is made).

PiholeApiToken.description: A freshly issued token: shown once.

token.description: The token. It is not stored and can't be read again: rotate to get another.

reason.description:
Why, in a few words (1 to 200 characters, one line): shown on the Cluster page, in the
`cluster_pinned` alert, and in the audit log.
reason.example: the new upstream group breaks banking sites

body.description: The write's body as shown: credentials read `<redacted>` (API-014).

configVersion.description: The configuration version the plan was made against.

method.description: The REST write it replays: `PUT` or `DELETE`.

preview.description: The dry run's answer: before, after, impact, and warnings.

reason.description: Why the agent wants it (goes into the audit log).

result.description: The write's answer once applied (or why it failed).

state.description:
`pending` (waits for an operator), `ready`, `approved`, `rejected`, `applying`,
`applied`, `stale` (the configuration changed), `failed`, `discarded`, or `expired`.

summary.description: What it does, in one sentence.

tool.description: The MCP tool that made it, e.g. `plan_block_domain`.

PolicyItem.description: One line of a section: a list, a service, a schedule, a rule, a rewrite, an upstream group.

from.description: What gives the device this line: `group kids`, `device`, `everyone`, `a schedule`.

oneOf.description: Where to change it.

state.description:
`on`, `off`, `in_effect`, `not_in_effect`, `not_applied`, `expired`, `shadow`, or absent when a line has no
state of its own.

untilUnixSeconds.description: When it stops applying (a rule's expiry), Unix seconds.

PolicyLink.description: A page in the UI a line comes from.

PolicyRung.description: One rung of the identification ladder (ADR-973, ADR-976).

source.description:
`client_id`, `edns_mac`, `neighbor_mac`, `kubernetes`, `ip`, `cidr`, `router_name`, `default`
(the values Explain's `identifiedBy` uses).

PolicySection.description: A titled group of lines. Sections are the panel's unit; it renders whatever arrives, in order.

oneOf.description: Where the whole section is edited.

summary.description: One sentence that stands alone (T35.2): it names the group and the count, and never points at the page ("below", "these"), so the API and an agent read it as it is.
summary.example: Group kids uses the 3 lists it names.

ProbeResult.description:
REQ: OBS-020 (ADR-107) — one synthetic probe: a DNS listener asked through its own
protocol, or an extra target, from one node, and the listener's certificate.

certError.description: Why the certificate couldn't be read.

certExpiresUnixSeconds.description: A TLS listener's certificate: when it expires and the days left (negative: expired).

certNames.description: The names and addresses the certificate covers.

certSelfSigned.description:
WrenDNS made the certificate itself (`[api] tls = { self_signed = true }`); it
doesn't expire.

certSha256.description:
The certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint (colon-separated hex), to compare with the one a
browser shows before trusting it.

consecutiveFailures.description: Probes failed in a row (2 or more degrade the health level).

lastOkUnixSeconds.description: When it last answered, and when it was last asked (Unix seconds).

listener.description: One of this node's listeners (else an extra `[probe] targets` entry).

node.description: The node that probed (cluster nodes only).

ok.description: The last probe got a well-formed answer (any response code).

proto.description:
`udp`, `tcp`, `dot`, `doh`, `doh3`, or `doq`; or `api`: the web UI and API over HTTPS
(`[api] tls`, ADR-149), checked with a `GET /livez`.

skipped.description: Not probed, and why (a listener that requires the PROXY protocol header).

detail.description: What went wrong in this request.

diff.description:
REQ: CLU-013 — with `cluster_pinned`: what the pin holds back, as JSON Patch operations
from the pinned version's shared configuration to the one this node would publish.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary of the problem type.

example.detail: `from`: `yesterday`: expected RFC 3339 time (2026-10-03T12:00:00Z) or a relative offset (-24h)
example.hint: Use a relative offset such as -24h, or RFC 3339 such as 2026-10-03T00:00:00Z.
example.title: Invalid parameter

ProfileKey.description: One way to recognize a device.

randomized.description: A MAC with the locally administered bit (a private Wi-Fi address, ADR-910): it may change.

value.description: As a `[[client]] match` key is written (`aa:bb:..`, `192.168.1.5`, `hostname:tv`).

ProfileSource.description: A network or a device the picker offers (REQ: FLT-902).

configured.description: A configured device (a `[[client]]`), as opposed to one only seen.

definedIn.description: Where the device is defined: `file` (read-only) or `api`.

group.description: The group a device is in now (its effective group), or the group that holds a network.

id.description: What to write: a CIDR for a network, a configured device's name, or a seen device's address.

keys.description: The keys the device can be selected by.

label.description: The name to show: a network's name, a device's name or its address.

PromotePlan.description: What promoting this node would do (`POST /cluster/promote?dryRun=true`, AGT-002).

emergency.description: It would coordinate without publishing new configuration (ADR-048).

epoch.description: The epoch this node would take.

impact.description: What would happen, in one sentence.

emergency.description:
Promote even though this node can't publish configuration under the cluster's
authority (configuration from Git, and no Git-managed node reachable): it coordinates the
cluster and keeps the last version, and publishes nothing new (ADR-048).

password.description:
From a signed-in session: your password, to confirm (`spec/12` §5). Not needed with
an API token or for `dryRun`.

totp.description: From a signed-in session with two-factor sign-in on: the current code.

nodes.description: By stage (groups, statuses, upstreams, response codes), largest first.

partial.description:
Some buckets had answers but no joint counts (stored by an older build, or a node that
doesn't count them yet): their answers are missing here.

source.description: `buckets` (the time buckets' joint counts) or `querylog` (one device's rows).

total.description: Answers in the window (group → status links add up to it).

truncated.description:
The query log read stopped early, or had more combinations than it returns: the numbers
cover what it read.

QueryPage.description: A page of query-log rows, newest first.

clientTruncated.description:
REQ: FLT-017 — `client` named a Kubernetes workload that held more than 64 pod
addresses in the window: only the newest 64 were searched.

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read (CLU-002: partial results, never a hang).

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get older rows; absent when there are none.

scanned.description: How much of the log this page looked at.

clientName.description: The configured device name, when known.

list.description: The list whose rule blocked or allowed the query.

node.description: The node that answered it (federated reads: its site).

rcode.description: Response code, or null when nothing was sent.

RecordInput.description: One record of a local name.

nodeOnly.description: REQ: CLU-006 (T27.7) — keep this record on this node only (a cluster doesn't share it).

value.description:
An address for A/AAAA, a name for CNAME/PTR, text for TXT, `"10 mail.home.arpa"` for MX,
`"0 5 5060 pbx.home.arpa"` for SRV.

RecursorTrace.description: How a recursive lookup went, step by step (`GET /api/v1/recursor/trace`, REQ: DNS-904).

error.description: Why the lookup failed (answered SERVFAIL to a client), when it did.

rcode.description: The answer's code (`NOERROR`, `NXDOMAIN`); absent when the lookup failed.

steps.description: The steps, in order. At most 128.

totalMicros.description: From the first step to the last, in microseconds.

RecursorTraceStep.description: One line of a recursive lookup's trace (REQ: DNS-904).

detail.description:
The zone a referral delegates to, the target of a CNAME answer, or how many servers a
start had; empty otherwise.

kind.description: `start` (where the lookup began) or `query` (one query to one server).

outcome.description:
A query: `referral`, `answer`, `nodata`, `nxdomain`, `lame`, `timeout`, `error` or
`case-mismatch`. A start: `cache`, `stub` or `root`.

qname.description: The name asked: a prefix of the full name while the name is being cut down (RFC 9156).

zone.description: The zone whose servers were asked (`start`: the zone the lookup began at).

answer.description: An address, or a name (answered as a CNAME).

dominantBin.description: The bin holding most of `recent`, and its share (percent).

hour.description: This hour's gaps per bin (24 counts; see `binsS`).

knownPeriodic.description: It was periodic while the device was learning: its usual behaviour.

nodes.description: The cluster nodes that track it.

period.description: In words, when one bin holds at least half: `every 2.5 s`, `every 5 min`, `in bursts`.

recent.description: The recent view: each hour's close halves it and adds that hour; this hour included.

regularHours.description: Consecutive hours the beacon detector found it regular (4 reports a new beacon).

typicalGapS.description: The mean of the latest gaps in whole seconds (1 s to an hour), when there are enough.

RolloutAction.description: REQ: CLU-013 — what a rollout or pin action did (or, as a dry run, would do).

configVersion.description:
The configuration version the action was checked against (plans send it back in
`If-Match`).

diff.description:
For a pin: what changes on every node, as JSON Patch from the version served now to
the pinned one, and one sentence per section.

RolloutFailure.description: REQ: CLU-013 — a version the guard failed.

RolloutNode.description: REQ: CLU-013 — one node during a rollout.

canary.description: Whether it's a canary (of the rollout in progress, or under the settings).

servfailPercent.description: Its SERVFAIL share now, in percent.

RolloutStatus.description:
REQ: CLU-013 — `GET /api/v1/cluster/rollout`: the rollout in progress, the guard, and the
pin.

canaries.description:
`[cluster.rollout] canaries`: node IDs, `site:<name>`, or `ephemeral`; empty means
changes reach every node at once.

fromPrimary.description:
Whether the answer comes from the primary (a replica that can't reach it shows what it
knows from the version it applied).

oneOf.description: The guard's readings so far, or of the last decision.

rolloutCanaries.description: The canary nodes the version went to.

skipped.description: Why the last change went to every node at once although canaries are set.

stable.description: The version every node runs (or is getting), `epoch.seq`.

stage.description:
`none`, `canary` (a version is baking), `waiting` (canaries are set and none is online:
the change goes to every node after a minute), or `pinned`.

started.description: When the bake began and ends (RFC 3339), and the seconds left.

waitingSince.description: Since when a change has waited for a canary (RFC 3339).

RouterCertificate.description:
REQ: API-016 (T23.8) — a router's certificate as the console presents it
(`POST /checks/router-certificate`).

fingerprintSha256.description: SHA-256 of the DER, as colon-separated hex.

names.description: The names it carries (subject and subject alternative names).

pem.description: The PEM text, ready to paste into `tls_ca_pem`.

suggestedTlsServerName.description:
The name to set as `tls_server_name` when the certificate names something other than the
address.

RouterCheck.description: REQ: API-016 (T23.8) — a read-only poll of a router as a draft (`POST /checks/router`).

credentialSent.description:
Whether a stored credential went to the address (it's sent only to the address it was
saved for; see the check's help).

error.description: Why it failed, with the address's password removed.

RouterCredential.description: REQ: API-016 (T23.7) — one credential field of a router and where it stands on this node.

issue.description: Why it can't be used here (named, never valued), when it can't.

readable.description: Whether this node can read it now; `None` when nothing is set.

secret.description: The stored secret's name, when `source` is `stored`.

source.description: `file` (read as it is), `stored` (the encrypted store, by name), or `none`.

RouterEntry.description:
REQ: API-016 (T23.7, ADR-921) — one router integration as the API shows it: its settings
(secrets as names, never values), where it comes from, and what this node's poll of it did.

credentials.description: Each credential this entry uses, where it comes from, and whether this node can read it.

definition.description: The settings in effect: the `[[router]]` fields as JSON, with `*_ref` names.

setByFile.description: The fields the configuration files set (`api_key_file`, `tls_ca`...), shown as set by file.

source.description: `file` (the configuration files define it; read-only here) or `api`.

url.description: The address, with any password in it removed (API-014).

missingNodes.description:
REQ: API-016 (T24.41) - the primary, when this node reads routers through it and it
didn't answer (the statuses are this node's own then).

RouterStatus.description: REQ: API-016 (T23.7) — what this node's poll of a router last did.

error.description: Why the last read failed (the address has no password in it).

lastPoll.description: Unix seconds of the last read attempt.

polledBy.description:
`this node`, `the primary` (a stored credential polls there only), or `skipped` with the
reason (a resolver pod).

readBy.description:
REQ: API-016 (T24.41) - the node whose read this status is, when it is not the node that
answered: a replica shows the primary's state of a router only the primary reads.

state.description: `waiting` (not read yet), `ok`, `failing` (keeping the last answer), or `skipped`.

RuleInfo.description: A quick rule (files and API), with how long it has left.

expiresInSeconds.description: Seconds until it expires (0 once it has).

source.description: `file` (read-only here) or `api`.

RuleInput.description:
REQ: FLT-005 (T6.12, ADR-067) — a quick rule to create or replace
(`PUT /api/v1/rules/{id}`).

devices.description: Device names, IPs, or CIDRs it applies to.

domain.description: The domain; its subdomains are included.

expires.description: When it stops applying (RFC 3339). Use this or `forMinutes`; neither means never.

forMinutes.description: Stop applying this many minutes from now.

groups.description: Groups it applies to. With neither devices nor groups: everyone.

note.description: Why it exists, shown with every decision it makes.

Scope.description: An API token's scope; a token never exceeds its owner's role.

SecretChange.description: REQ: API-015, AGT-002 — what a `PUT` or `DELETE` did (or, with `dryRun`, would do).

head.description: The head after the change (its `etag` for the next `If-Match`).

usedBy.description: The fields that name it: they become configured with it (or lose it, on delete).

SecretMember.description:
REQ: API-015 (T24.42) - one cluster member's part in `GET /api/v1/secrets`: the same list on
every node.

held.description: How many stored secrets it holds (0 unless it answered).

kind.description:
`full` (holds every stored secret), `resolver` (a resolver pod: holds none, by design) or
`witness` (votes only: holds none, by design).

node.description: As the Cluster page names it.

state.description: `answered`, `unknown` (a full member that didn't answer, or is too old to), or `not_held`.

SecretMeta.description: A stored secret: never its value.

health.description: On the answering node: `readable`, `unreadable` (another key made it) or `corrupt`.

nodes.description: Which nodes hold it, and whether they can read it.

set.description: Stored now (false: a reference names it but it isn't set, or it was deleted).

updated.description: When it was set or deleted (RFC 3339).

usedBy.description: The credential fields that name it.

SecretNode.description: How one node holds a secret.

oneOf.description:
The stamp it holds (never a value or a hash of one); absent when it holds none or didn't
answer.

state.description:
REQ: API-015 (T24.42) - how this member holds it: `applied` (the stamp the list shows,
readable), `unreadable`, `behind` (an older stamp), `ahead` (a newer one), `missing`, or
`unknown` (the member didn't answer, or is too old to say). Absent from an older node.

unreadable.description: It holds it but can't read it (another key made it, or it's damaged).

kind.description: `text` (the default) or `pem` (PEM blocks, with their line breaks; never shown again).

value.description:
The value: one line of text (a token, a password, an API key), at most 8 KiB, trimmed, no
control characters. Write-only: no answer, read, log, audit entry or backup without a
passphrase ever holds it.

SecretStamp.description: A stamp: the epoch (0 on a standalone node) and the change's number in it.

SecretUse.description: A credential field that names a secret.

name.description: The entry's name (`default` for the Git source and OTLP).

node.description: The node whose own (node-local) configuration holds the reference; absent: the cluster's.

source.description: `stored`: the field takes the secret.

SecretsHead.description:
REQ: API-015 (ADR-903 §2) — the secrets head: the highest stamp and a digest of every
secret's name, kind, stamp and deletion (no value, no value hash). `etag` is what `If-Match`
takes.

etag.description: `"<epoch>.<seq>.<first 16 digits of digest>"`: send it as `If-Match`.

items.description: Stored secrets (and names a reference uses that aren't set), by name.

members.description:
REQ: API-015 (T24.42) - every member of the cluster and whether it holds the secrets, the
same on every node. Empty on a standalone node.

missingNodes.description: Full members that did not answer (offline, or an older version): their state is `unknown`.

stale.description: From this node's own copy: the primary couldn't be asked.

warnings.description: A full member that lacks a secret, holds an older one or can't read it, in words.

dataEphemeral.description: The data directory isn't kept across restarts (stored secrets would be lost).

keySource.description: Where the key came from (the environment, or a file's path); never the key.

state.description: `starting`, `ready`, `locked`, or `ephemeral` (a resolver pod: it holds none).

domains.description: The domains it blocks (with everything under them).

ShadowListStats.description:
REQ: OBS-018 (ADR-109) — what a `shadow` list would have blocked (it never does), since
the node started (every node's, merged, in a cluster).

devices.description: Devices those queries came from (each node counts its own; capped at 4,096 per node).

hits.description: Queries it would have blocked (answered normally instead).

nodes.description: The nodes that counted (cluster nodes only).

since.description: When counting started (RFC 3339): the earliest node's start, in a cluster.

topNames.description: The names it would have blocked most (hashed at privacy level 1 and above).

config.description:
The candidate shared configuration, as JSON: the shape a Git commit's shared TOML
becomes (node-local sections are ignored; this node's own apply).

until.description: The end of the window (RFC 3339 or relative, e.g. `-1h`); default now.

window.description: How far back: `30m`, `24h`, `7d` (at most 7 days). Default `[simulate] default_window`.

SimulatedClass.description:
One kind of difference: how many queries, from how many devices, and the names most
affected (at most 20, most first).

list.description:
What decided: the list (or quick rule, schedule) that blocks or had blocked it, the
route change, or the new answer.

Simulation.description:
REQ: OBS-024 (T13.1, ADR-115) — what a configuration change would have done to the queries
already in the query log: each logged query decided again under the current configuration
and under the candidate, and the differences counted. Decisions only: nothing is asked of
upstreams, and caching, DNSSEC, rate limits, pauses, and CNAME-target blocks aren't replayed.
About the past: names nobody asked in the window count for nothing.

applicable.description:
False for a change that can't affect a decision (alerts, users, exclusions): nothing
was read.

available.description:
False when it couldn't run (`reason` says why: `disabled`, `privacy_level`,
`no_query_log`, `busy`, ...).

byDevice.description: The devices most affected, most first (at most 50).

changedAnswer.description:
Answered differently without a block: a local record, a rewrite, no IPv6 addresses, a
special answer (`list` describes the new answer).

changedRoute.description: Forwarded to another upstream group (`list` says from where to where).

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes whose queries aren't included (they didn't answer).

newlyAllowed.description: Blocked now, allowed under the change (`list` names the list that had blocked it).

newlyBlocked.description: Allowed now, blocked under the change.

partial.description: Stopped early (`[simulate] max_rows` or `max_secs`): the counts cover the newest `rows`.

rows.description: Logged queries read (on every node that answered).

undetermined.description:
At privacy level 1 (names hashed), queries of devices whose group changes to one with
different settings: they can't be decided again without the names.

SinkEntry.description:
REQ: API-016, OBS-010 (T23.11, ADR-984) — one event sink in the configuration: its settings
(a stored token as a name, never a value), where it comes from, and what this node does with it.

definition.description: The settings in effect: the `[[telemetry.sink]]` fields as JSON, with `token_ref` named.

dropped.description: Events dropped since this node started (the buffer was full, or a batch was refused).

location.description:
Where events go: the file, the syslog address or the webhook URL (a password in it
removed, API-014).

reason.description: Why it doesn't (a resolver pod holds no stored secrets; its settings couldn't be used).

running.description: Whether the sink's thread runs on this node.

source.description: `file` (the configuration files define it; read-only here) or `api`.

token.description: The stored secret's name, when `tokenSource` is `stored`.

tokenReadable.description: Whether this node can read the token now; absent when none is set.

tokenSource.description:
Where the webhook token comes from: `stored` (the encrypted store, by name), `file`, or
`none`.

filesDir.description:
Where a file sink made in the UI writes: the file name it is given goes under this
directory on every node.

SloAttribution.description: REQ: OBS-027 — who and what spent an objective's error budget.

note.description: A plain note, such as few answers making one failure move the ratio a lot.

timeline.description: Per node and hour (or day), oldest first.

SloBurn.description:
REQ: OBS-016 — the error budget's burn rate over one window: the bad share divided by the
share the target allows (1 spends exactly the budget over the objective's window).

rate.description: None when there were no answers (or no hourly data for `3d`).

total.description: Answers in the window, and bad ones.

SloObjective.description:
REQ: OBS-016 — one objective: `availability` (answers that aren't SERVFAIL) or `latency`
(answers within `latencyMs`). Dropped queries got no answer and count for neither.

alert.description:
`fast` (14.4× over 1h and 5m), `slow` (6× over 6h and 30m), or `ticket` (1× over 3d
and 6h); none when the budget lasts. `fast` and `slow` degrade the health level and
fire `slo_burn` alerts.

budgetRemainingPercent.description: The window's error budget left, in percent: 100 untouched, 0 spent, below 0 overspent.

good.description: Good and all answers over the window.

goodMeans.description: What counts as a good answer, in words.

sliPercent.description: Good answers over the window, in percent (none: no answers yet).

targetPercent.description: The share of good answers aimed for, in percent.

SloStatus.description:
REQ: OBS-016 (ADR-105) — the service-level objectives, their error budgets, and how fast
they're being spent, over every node's answers.

enabled.description: `[slo] enabled`; when false there are no objectives.

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that didn't answer (their answers aren't counted).

windowDays.description: Days each error budget covers (`[slo] window_days`).

SnmpTestOid.description: REQ: DSC-004 — one table root a test would query (or did).

alternative.description: The MIB table (an alternative; the first that answers is used).

columns.description: The column OIDs a poll walks when this alternative answers.

part.description: The part of the table group.

probeOid.description: The OID the probe's one GETNEXT starts from.

SnmpTestRequest.description:
REQ: DSC-004 (T25.6, ADR-908, ADR-1002) — `POST /api/v1/discovery/snmp/test`: the agent to
test, by name. No address is ever accepted (ADR-907).

agent.description: The agent's name, from `[[discovery.snmp_agent]]` (`GET /api/v1/discovery/status` lists them).

oneOf.description: What the agent answered (not for a dry run, or a test that failed).

dryRun.description: True when no packet was sent (`?dryRun=true`): `oids` is what a test would query.

durationMs.description: How long the test took, in milliseconds.

error.description: Why the test failed, in words.

node.description: The node that ran the test (the designated node, which may not be the one asked).

note.description: What happens next, in a sentence.

oids.description: The OIDs a test queries: one GETNEXT on each probe root, one GET of sysObjectID.

ok.description: Whether the agent answered (a dry run is always `true`).

SourceState.description: Where a source stands on this node.

alsoIn.description: The lists that have the rest, most shared first (at most three).

downloaded.description: False until a group uses it and it has downloaded.

list.description: The list the node keeps it in (`cat-<id>`, or a file's list with the same URL).

providedBy.description:
A list the config files define has this source's URL, so nothing is downloaded twice and
the checkbox says "provided by list X, set by file".

snapshotEntries.description:
REQ: FLT-004 (T24.28, ADR-992) — names this source puts in the active snapshot, and how
many of them no other enabled list has (zero while it is not downloaded and compiled).

SourceView.description: One source, with its licence and size.

attribution.description: A line shown next to the checkbox (CC BY-SA sources).

checked.description: The catalog's check date and the maintainer's last push on it.

entries.description: From the file's header when the catalog was built.

refreshSeconds.description: How often this node refreshes it.

activeClients.description:
Distinct clients seen in the hours the range overlaps (REQ: OBS-004): this hour's list,
the previous hour's, and each stored hour's busiest 100, so ranges past the last two
hours undercount on networks with more than 100 devices an hour.

cacheHitPercent.description: Cache share of answered queries that weren't blocked or local, 0–100.

cached.description: Answered from cache (fresh, refreshed in the background, or stale).

latency.description: Latency percentiles this hour, by answer path (`cache`, `upstream`, ...).

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read (CLU-002).

refreshed.description:
REQ: DNS-007 — of `cached`, answers whose entry had expired and was answered at once
while it was refreshed in the background (`[cache] stale_answer_client_timeout_ms = 0`).

Supervisor.description: How a node is supervised (ADR-956 §4a): from a declaration only.

how.description: How the node knows: `WRENDNS_SUPERVISOR`, or `not declared`.

SupportPackageRequest.description: REQ: OPS-011 (ADR-156) — `POST /system/support-package`: what the package should hold.

cluster.description:
REQ: OPS-011 (ADR-172) — one package for the whole cluster: every reachable node makes and
redacts its own part under one key made for this package, so a device has the same
pseudonym on every node and no real name or address leaves the node it is on. Not with
`keepMap` (the names never leave their nodes, so there is no map). A node that doesn't
answer, or is older than this feature, is listed in the manifest.

keepMap.description: Keep the pseudonym map in memory for one download (`GET /system/support-package/{id}/map`).

level.description: `strict` (the default), `standard`, or `none`: how much is obfuscated.

querySample.description: Rows of the query log to include, newest first (0 to 1,000; `standard` and `none` only).

reveal.description: Names (a device, a group, a node, a host) to keep readable. At most 50.

addresses.description:
REQ: UPS-013 (T24.31, ADR-997) — this node's own interface addresses (loopback and
link-local left out), which an upstream's `source` can name. They differ per node.

oneOf.description:
Present when client IPs appear masked (OPS-003): most recent queries come from a few
infrastructure addresses (a Kubernetes node, a Docker bridge, a forwarding router),
so per-device statistics and rules see those instead of devices.
Present when this node belongs to a cluster (CLU-001).

filterNames.description: Blocked names in the active snapshot.

filterSnapshot.description: Version of the active filter snapshot, if one is loaded.

listenerAccess.description:
REQ: DNS-901 (T36.2) — each listener's known-ID gate: whether it requires a device key
and whether it is bound to a public address, so the UI can warn about an open one.

oneOf.description: REQ: OPS-010 — this node's maintenance window, while it's in maintenance.

node.description: Node name.

queryLog.description: Whether the per-query log is being written.

starts.description:
REQ: OBS-002 (T9.13) — times a node started on this data directory, and how many of
those followed a run that didn't stop cleanly.

update.description: Whether a newer build exists on this build's channel (ADR-046).

TailDropped.description: Sent as an SSE `dropped` event when matching queries weren't delivered.

dropped.description: How many matching queries were skipped since the last report.

reason.description: `rate`: over this subscriber's `rate`; `lag`: the subscriber fell behind.

sources.description: The sources this tier adds or switches to.

byGroup.description: Queries by the client's group (ADR-050). Empty for buckets read from rollups.

flow.description:
REQ: OBS-032 — the query flow's joint counts: `gs:<group>/<status>` (every answer),
`su:<status>/<upstream>` and `ur:<upstream>/<rcode>` (answers an upstream was asked for),
`sr:<status>/<rcode>` (the rest with a response code). Minute and longer buckets; empty
before 0.5.

latencyHist.description:
REQ: OBS-030 — answers per latency bucket (the `wrendns_query_duration_seconds` bounds
and the overflow, 17 counts) by path (`cache`, `upstream`, `local`, `synthesized`) and
by upstream (`upstream:<name>`). Minute and longer buckets; empty before 0.5.

servfailByStatus.description:
REQ: OBS-027 — SERVFAIL answers by status (`refreshed`, `forwarded`, ...). Empty in
buckets without any, or stored by builds before 0.5.

servfailByUpstream.description:
REQ: OBS-027 — SERVFAIL answers by the upstream that gave them (`none`: no upstream on
the answer, such as one served from the cache).

slow.description:
REQ: OBS-016 — answered queries slower than the latency objective's threshold
(`[slo] latency_ms`). 0 in buckets stored by builds before 0.4.

slowByRcode.description: REQ: OBS-027 — slow answers by response code.

slowByStatus.description: REQ: OBS-027 — slow answers (see `slow`) by status.

slowByUpstream.description: REQ: OBS-027 — slow answers by upstream.

upstreamQueries.description: Upstream exchanges, and how many failed.

TimelineEvent.description: Something that happened to or on the device.

href.description: The UI page that shows it (`#/…`).

counts.description:
Queries, blocked answers, and slow answers (over the latency objective's threshold) per
bin.

domain.description: The registrable domain; `other` for the rest; absent at privacy level 1 (names hashed).

firstSeenTime.description: When the device first contacted it, if that's inside the window (RFC 3339).

other.description: The lane folds every domain below the top ones.

group.description: For agent tokens: restricted to this client group.

ratePerMinute.description: For agent tokens: requests per minute (default: `[agents] rate_per_minute`).

scope.description: For user tokens. Agent tokens show the closest equivalent.

scopes.description: For agent tokens: what it may do (e.g. `analytics:read`, `config:write:clients`).

TokenKind.description: Whether a token is for a person's scripts or for an agent (AGT-004).

TopHour.description: Which window a top list reads: an hour, or (clients only) the last 60 minutes.

TopItem.description:
One ranked item. Counts come from a Space-Saving sketch: the true count lies in
`[count - errorBound, count]`.

oneOf.description:
For clients: how its queries were answered (REQ: OBS-004). Counts cover the queries
since the client entered the list, `count - errorBound` of them; the rest of `count`
is other statuses (local, special, refused, …) and that error bound.

groups.description:
For clients: the groups whose settings apply to it, highest priority first (its
device's groups, else its network's group, else the default; ADR-050).

name.description: The configured device name, for clients that have one.

secretBase32.description: For manual entry in an authenticator app.

UnstableVoter.description: REQ: CLU-005 (T24.38, ADR-1018) — a voter this node reaches only some of the time.

drops.description:
How many times its link dropped within `windowSeconds` (not counting a drop the voter
came back from as a restarted process).

UpdateStatus.description: Update status from the signed release index (ADR-046).

checkedUnixSeconds.description: When the index was last read successfully (Unix seconds).

how.description: How to update this install, step by step.

latest.description: The newest version on this channel, when known.

state.description:
`up_to_date`, `available`, `newer` (this build is newer than the index, e.g. dev),
`off` (`[updates] check = false`), or `unknown` (not checked yet, or failing).

password.description: Set a new password (ends the user's sessions).

resetTotp.description: Turn off the user's TOTP (if they lost their device).

UpstreamChecks.description:
REQ: OBS-019 (ADR-108) — one node's view of its upstreams' answers: second opinions
(sampled, `[upstream_check]`), DNSSEC verdicts, and the EDE codes they returned.

node.description: The node (cluster nodes only).

reference.description: The upstream group asked (none: another member of the answering group).

sampleEvery.description: One forwarded question in this many gets a second opinion.

UpstreamDisagreement.description: REQ: OBS-019 — two upstreams that answered the same question differently.

name.description: The name (hashed at privacy level 1 and above) and type.

UpstreamInfo.description: An upstream server and its health.

failuresByKind.description:
`failures` by kind, which say what to fix: timeouts point at the path or the upstream's
load, network errors at the connection, SERVFAIL at the domain asked about.

id.description: Stable ID (config order, from 1); query rows and latency rows refer to it.

routeProblem.description:
REQ: UPS-006 — why this node can't reach it, when it can say: `this node has no IPv6
route` (or IPv4). Checked at start and every 30 s with a `connect()` that sends nothing.

source.description:
REQ: UPS-013 (T24.31, ADR-997) — the local address its sockets are bound to, when the
upstream sets a `source`.

sourceProblem.description: REQ: UPS-013 — set while this node no longer holds that address: its queries fail.

UpstreamPreset.description: REQ: UPS-004 (T24.36) — a public resolver variant the simple picker offers.

note.description: One line: what it filters and what it does with your queries.

params.description: Placeholders in its addresses (a NextDNS profile); empty for every simple preset.

provider.description: The heading it is listed under (`Cloudflare`).

simple.description: Offered in the simple view (false: it needs a parameter, or is for the Advanced view).

UpstreamPresetEndpoint.description: REQ: UPS-004 (T24.36) — one address a public resolver answers on.

family.description: `v4` or `v6` for an address, `name` for a host name (which resolves to either).

tlsServerName.description: The name on the server certificate, for a `tls://` address given by IP.

UpstreamPresets.description: REQ: UPS-004 (T24.36) — the catalog, and what this node can reach.

ipv6Route.description:
Whether this node has a usable IPv6 default route: without one, an IPv6 upstream only
times out. Unknown (another OS) reads true.

UpstreamQuality.description: REQ: OBS-019 — one upstream's answers since start.

dnssecSecure.description: DNSSEC verdicts on its answers (when `[dnssec] mode` validates).

ede.description: The Extended DNS Error codes in its answers (RFC 8914).

same.description:
Second opinions by outcome: the same answer; different addresses (CDNs and geo-DNS
do this); a different response code; filtered (one side had addresses, the other none
or only 0.0.0.0/loopback); the second upstream didn't answer.

oidcProvider.description: The sign-in provider for users created by OIDC sign-in (they have no password here).

estimatedRows.description: Before scanning, from block headers: how many logged queries could match at most.

rowsScanned.description: What the scan did (0 for a dry run).

columns.description:
`time` (with `bucket`), the keys (a `client` key adds `clientName`), then the
statistics. Latencies are in ms.

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes whose query log isn't here (not shipped to this node).

note.description: Something to know about the answer (a window longer than the query log keeps).

query.description: The query as understood, with the defaults filled in.

rows.description: One array per row, in column order.

source.description:
REQ: AGT-012 (T9.12) — where the numbers come from: `querylog` (every query, kept
`retention_days`) or `rollups` (counts by one breakdown, kept much longer).

truncated.description: The scan stopped early (`truncatedReason` says why); the numbers cover what it read.

WorkloadEvidence.description: REQ: FLT-017 — a workload's identity, from the Kubernetes API.

labels.description: `app.kubernetes.io/name` and `app.kubernetes.io/part-of`, when its pods have them.

WorkloadInfo.description:
REQ: FLT-017 (T15.1) — one Kubernetes workload: a device WrenDNS names, groups, and
watches (`GET /api/v1/kubernetes/workloads`).

group.description: Its group; absent: its network's group or `default`, like any device.

groupFrom.description:
Where the group came from: `pod_label`, `namespace_label`, `map`, `default_group`, or
`none`.

key.description:
Its analytics address (`100::/64`, RFC 6666): how top lists, anomalies, rhythm, and the
device timeline key it, across rollouts.

labels.description: `app.kubernetes.io/name` and `app.kubernetes.io/part-of`, when its pods have them.

lastSeen.description: When it last asked (RFC 3339), within the last day.

pods.description: Its pods now (a deleted one stays 30 seconds, `terminating`).

queries24h.description: Queries and blocked answers in the last 24 hours (every node's, in a cluster).

WorkloadPage.description: REQ: FLT-017 — a page of workloads, by name.

missingNodes.description: Nodes whose counts are missing (the table itself is the watcher's, on every node).

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last.

total.description: Workloads matching the filters, on every page.

WorkloadPod.description: REQ: FLT-017 — one pod of a workload.

terminating.description: Deleted: its addresses stay its own for 30 seconds (queries in flight).

WorldMarker.description: An upstream placed on the map.

WorldRegion.description: One country of the world view.

name.description: The code again: the console writes the country's name.

WorldUnlocated.description: Answers that have no place on the map, and why.

ZoneInfo.description: REQ: DNS-018 (T7.22) — an authoritative zone from `[[zone]]`.

file.description: The zone file, when it has one.

groups.description: Groups that see it (split horizon); empty: everyone.

negativeTtlSeconds.description: TTL of its NXDOMAIN and no-data answers.

records.description: Records loaded (from the file and inline).

source.description: REQ: DNS-010 (T27.7) — `file` (read-only here) or `api` (made in the UI or API).

values.description:
REQ: DNS-010 (T27.7) — an API zone's records, to edit them; empty for a file zone (its
records are read-only here, and only the count shows).

ZoneInput.description:
REQ: DNS-010 (T27.7) — an authoritative zone made through the API or UI
(`PUT /api/v1/zones/{name}`). The zone file is set in the configuration file (guarded, T27.17),
so a body that names one is refused.

groups.description: Groups that see the zone (split horizon); empty: everyone.

negativeTtlSeconds.description: TTL of its NXDOMAIN and no-data answers (default 300).

records.description: The zone's records: names under the zone.

ZoneRecordInput.description:
REQ: DNS-010 (T27.7) — one record of an API zone: the owner name, its type and value, and
an optional TTL.

tags.name: stats
tags.description: Counters, top lists, and latency percentiles. Live windows in memory (15 minutes per second, 48 hours per minute) plus rollups on disk (7 days per minute, 400 days per hour, days forever).

tags.name: queries
tags.description: The query log and explanations of decisions.

tags.name: map
tags.description: REQ: OBS-901 - the live network map: the gateway, networks, devices, WrenDNS nodes and upstreams, coloured by health, from a sample of the lookups (never from the query path).

tags.name: config
tags.description: Lists, groups, clients, and upstreams as running.

tags.name: agents
tags.description: Changes AI agents planned through MCP, and their approval.

tags.name: pihole-compat
tags.description: REQ: API-005 (T24.10, ADR-961) - the part of Pi-hole's v6             (`/api/...`) and v5 (`/admin/api.php`) interfaces that dashboards, phone apps and the             Home Assistant Pi-hole integration use. Off unless an admin turns it on (Settings,             Pi-hole); authenticated by its own token, not by the sign-in methods under the auth             tag; it reads the statistics and turns blocking off for a while and on again, and             changes nothing else.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Sign-in, two-factor, API tokens, and users. Everything else needs one of: the session cookie from POST /auth/login (plus X-CSRF-Token on changes), Authorization: Bearer <token>, or HTTP Basic for users who allow it.
